title: Asymptotic stability of high-index saddle dynamics
abstract: High-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) has been extensively adopted to compute saddle points of arbitrary index, with various applications such as constructing solution landscapes of complex systems. In this work, we prove the asymptotic stability of various HiSD methods, including the idealized, perturbed, and coupled HiSD methods, as well as their momentum-accelerated variants. The analysis is Jacobian-free and thus compensates for the linear stability analysis in the literature. The results not only provide specific characterizations for the convergence rate and the basin of attraction, but also reveal intrinsic correlations among dynamics in the coupled HiSD. Theoretical results are substantiated by numerical experiments.

title: On optimal convergence rates for parametrized variational problems with applications to nonlocal models
abstract: We develop an abstract variational framework for convergence rates of parametrized problems and their Galerkin approximations, with applications to nonlocal diffusion. The main objective is to quantify modeling and discretization errors in terms of the nonlocal horizon, the mesh size, the Sobolev regularity of the local solution, and the compatibility of boundary data. We establish error estimates in energy and $L^2$ norms and develop an adaptation of the Aubin--Nitsche argument that uses regularity of the limiting local dual problem. This approach yields improved $L^2$ estimates without requiring additional regularity of the nonlocal dual solutions, including for integrable kernels. We apply the framework to two constant-horizon nonlocal Laplacians with exterior boundary data and to heterogeneous localization models with classical Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions. The resulting estimates provide quantitative guarantees of asymptotic compatibility and improve existing error bounds under weaker regularity assumptions. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence rates and examine the sharpness of the estimates.

title: Stabilizing Vector Approximate Message Passing with Circuit-Designed Lag-Lead Damping
abstract: Vector approximate message passing (VAMP) often fails to converge on ill-conditioned matrices, and its damping factor is tuned either manually or adaptively. Using the fact that VAMP iterations are the discretization of an electric circuit, we show that the denoiser and the likelihood act as nonlinear resistors, the Onsager correction is a mirror resistor and damping is a lag filter. This circuit gives a closed-form loop gain whose spectrum can predict when VAMP fails. Because a lag filter cannot isolate the oscillating modes, we add a lead capacitor whose design often results in a negative capacitance. Across a wide range of condition numbers, our proposed damping strategy achieves a higher convergence rate than adaptive damping and Anderson acceleration at a lower mean iteration cost. On ill-conditioned multipath channels, across ranks and sparsity levels, it also converges more reliably than existing damping baselines.

title: Composite witness sieves, Kneser--Plancherel containers, and the exponent $5/7$ for the Erdős--Straus conjecture
abstract:
For the Erdős--Straus equation $4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z$, Vaughan's unconditional bound on the exceptional set $E(N)$ has stood at $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c(\log N)^{2/3})$ since 1970. We harness composite divisor witnesses at growing depth to cross this $2/3$ barrier unconditionally. On the full exceptional set $E(N)$, we prove the unconditional bound $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c'(\log N)^{5/7}/(\log\log N)^{2/7})$, improving the exponent to $5/7$ (with an intermediate stage at $7/10$). On the structured component $E_2^{\mathrm{small}}(N;J(N))$, an algebraic and spectral container hierarchy combined with a generating-polynomial large sieve reaches the exponent $1-o(1)$: $|E_2^{\mathrm{small}}(N;J(N))|\ll_κN\exp(-(\frac{1}{40960}+o(1))\frac{\log N}{(\log\log N)(\log\log\log N)^κ})$, matching the CRT capacity scale.
  These results resolve the obstructions to composite-witness sieving at growing depth. First, we replace subgroup generation by Kneser's stabilizer $K(M)$, which embeds into a $2$-primary character kernel, reducing container counts from $2^{Θ(J^{4})}$ to $\exp(\mathcal{O}(J^{2}\log\log J))$. Coupling this with a generating-polynomial large sieve, Markov $1/2$-popular symmetry containers, and Pontryagin--Plancherel character containers yields the exponent $1-o(1)$ on $E_2^{\mathrm{small}}$. Second, to bypass unlocalized diffuse divisor sheets without subset enumeration, we construct a semi-composite congruence sieve $s=pq\equiv-1\pmod{12ua}$ ($p\in(Z^{9/10},Z]$, $q\le Q$ rough). Conditioning on $n\bmod M_{\mathrm{small}}$ yields CRT mutual independence while decoupling the modulus $12ua\le 12Z^{1/4}$ from $q$; a Bonferroni majorant and the Bombieri--Vinogradov theorem then yield the unconditional $5/7$ exponent on all of $E(N)$. Finally, we study bilinear dispersion on $4uavw-4u^{2}v-w=n$ and difference sets $D(K_c)$.

title: Levenshtein-type bounds for $(a,b)$-avoiding spherical codes
abstract: We develop a Levenshtein-type linear programming framework (for maximal $s$-codes and for minimal energy) for $(a,b)$-avoiding spherical codes, that is, codes whose inner products between distinct points avoid $(a,b)$. We introduce and investigate signed measures that are positive definite up to an appropriate degree and yield stationary auxiliary linear programming polynomials and exact quadrature formulas. We give explicit conditions for positivity of the quadrature weights and sufficient Krein-type conditions for nonnegative Gegenbauer coefficients (positive definiteness of the candidate optimal linear programming polynomials). Under these hypotheses and suitable node-location assumptions, the resulting cardinality bounds are optimal within the corresponding degree restriction and unique under natural nondegeneracy conditions. Under proper conditions on the quadrature nodes, we obtain universal lower energy bounds by utilizing Hermite interpolants as polynomial solutions of the respective linear program. Common test functions characterize optimality in the full polynomial linear programs under mild additional assumptions.

title: Regularity of Weak Solutions near Singular Minimizing Cones for the One-Phase Free Boundary Problem
abstract: Alt and Caffarelli proved an Allard-type $ε$-regularity theorem near the flat one-homogeneous minimizer of the one-phase free boundary problem. A natural follow-up question is whether an analogous regularity result holds near singular minimizing cones. In this paper, we prove such an $ε$-regularity theorem near a strongly integrable one-phase minimizing cone with an isolated singularity. More precisely, we show that, after a suitable translation and rotation, the free boundary of any non-degenerate weak solution sufficiently close to the cone is graphical over the free boundary of a leaf of the De Silva--Jerison--Shahgholian foliation. This result is analogous to recent $ε$-regularity theorems in minimal surface theory by Edelen and by Edelen--Spolaor; our proof adapts the strategy of Edelen to the one-phase setting.

title: Compressed Per-Player Local Methods for Multiplayer Federated Learning: Exact Convergence via Increment Sharing
abstract: Multiplayer Federated Learning (MpFL), introduced by Yoon et al. (2025), extends classical federated learning to settings where clients are rational players in a game with individual objectives and strategies, seeking an equilibrium. A natural baseline is Per-Player Local SGD (PEARL-SGD), where each player performs several local SGD steps before exchanging strategies through a central server. However, the original PEARL-SGD formulation does not extend cleanly to compressed communication. Directly compressing the players' strategies can prevent convergence to the equilibrium, even with deterministic gradients. To address this issue, we reformulate PEARL-SGD so that players communicate local strategy increments rather than the strategies themselves. Without compression, the two formulations are equivalent, but with compression, increment sharing preserves exact convergence, allowing us to design the communication-efficient compressed PEARL-SGD (C-PEARL-SGD). Beyond compression, we also consider variance reduction as another axis of improvement, introducing PEARL-SVRG and its compressed variant C-PEARL-SVRG. Under the original MpFL assumptions, we establish convergence guarantees for all variants through a unified parametric inequality. Numerical experiments, including distributed spectrum sensing, demonstrate the practical benefits of our methods over vanilla PEARL-SGD.

title: Evasive subspaces, minimal rank-metric codes and subspace designs via auxiliary fields
abstract: We extend the auxiliary-field method for scattered subspaces to evasive subspaces and subspace designs. For $1\le h\le k<hn$ and coprime $h,k+1$ with $n(k-h+1)\ge k+1$, we construct spanning $(h,k)$-evasive $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^r$ of dimension $rn(k-h+1)/(k+1)$ in every sufficiently large admissible ambient dimension, with a threshold independent of $q$. When $k<n$, this dimension is maximum. The proof combines an intersection lemma, a rank-support density inequality, scalar orbit counting, and a profile preserved by direct sums. The coding consequences include, for every fixed odd extension degree $m\ge3$ and every sufficiently large $K$, minimal rank-metric codes of optimal length $2K$ with first two generalized weights $(m+1)/2$ and $m+1$. For these codes the stable profile is equivalent to minimality with the largest possible minimum distance; for even $m$ the analogous class consists of minimal MRD codes. More generally, for $1\leτ\le m-2$ and $\gcd(m,τ+1)=1$, we obtain nondegenerate $τ$-minimal codes of length $(τ+1)K$ for every sufficiently large $K$, uniformly in $q$. We also construct maximum $h$-designs whose number of members grows exponentially with the ambient dimension at fixed $q,n,h$, and the associated maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes with a growing number of equal long blocks. In extension degree five, the ordinary and $2$-minimal constructions hold for every $q$ and every $K\ge32$ and $K\ge59$, respectively.

title: Rigidity, Regularity and Compactness of Special Lagrangian Submanifolds under Simons Stability
abstract: In this paper, we prove that, for suitable values of $δ$, every complete connected $δ$-Simons stable special Lagrangian immersion in ${\mathbb C}^n$, $n\ge3$, is flat. We also prove that a $δ$-Simons stable special Lagrangian cone $C\subset{\mathbb C}^n$ with $C\cap{\mathbb S}^{2n-1}$ smooth and compact is a finite union of planes if $δ>(n-2)^2/(4n)$, and that this coefficient is optimal. At equality, we characterize the $δ$-Simons stable cones. We further establish regularity and compactness for sequences of proper $δ$-Simons stable special Lagrangian immersions when $n\ge3$ and $δ>(n-2)/(n+1)$, under suitable restrictions on the initial singular sets, assuming integral current extensions $T_j$ with $\partial T_j=0$ and uniformly bounded mass on compact subsets. In dimension three, we allow initial singular sets $S_j$ satisfying $\mathcal H^1(S_j)=0$. For suitable values of $δ$, we also prove properness, Euclidean volume growth, and finite total curvature for complete connected immersions of finite $δ$-index.

title: Minimax designs and estimators for causal inference under network interference
abstract: We develop a design-based minimax theory for linear causal estimands under interference. We study the minimax risks of three problems: optimizing an estimator under a fixed design, optimizing an estimator and a design from a restricted class, or optimizing both over all designs. In each problem, we study the minimax risk over all estimators and over design-unbiased estimators separately. We allow any correctly specified exposure mapping, including the identity. Our theory represents causal inference under interference as a constrained sampling design on an expanded finite population of $\sum_i d_i$ potential outcomes, where $d_i$ is the number of exposure levels attainable by unit $i$. We describe the constrained sampling design by a weighted sampling hypergraph: its vertices are the potential outcomes, its hyperedges are the maximal sets of potential outcomes that can be jointly sampled under feasible treatment assignments, and its weights are induced by the randomization design. We show that the minimax risks of the fixed-design, restricted-design, and all-design problems depend, respectively, on the weighted hypergraph induced by the design, the collection of weighted hypergraphs attainable within the restricted class, and the unweighted hypergraph. Our Bayes lower bounds compare potential-outcome tables that differ on jointly missing sets of potential outcomes: joint-missingness probabilities govern the lower bounds over all estimators, whereas the corresponding odds govern the lower bounds over unbiased estimators. We illustrate the theory for average treatment effects without interference, saturation designs under partial interference, total, direct, and contagion effects under neighborhood interference, and bipartite dose-response contrasts. The upper and lower bounds match in several settings.

title: Fejer-Riesz factorization for free products
abstract: We establish an operator-valued Fejer-Riesz factorization theorem for the algebraic free product A of C[F], the group algebra on the free group F on finitely many generators, with finitely many finite dimensional C-star algebras. With respect to a natural reduced-word length, called extent, we show that every linear combination F of elements of A with coefficients from the algebra of operators on a Hilbert space of extent at most 2d that is positive under all finite-dimensional unital *-representations of A admits a factorization F=B^*B with B of extent at most d. This sharp half-extent bound holds without strict positivity. The proof combines a new finite-dimensional realization theorem for positive truncated kernels with operator-system methods. We also establish factorization results for tensor products with group algebras of arbitrary discrete groups under strict positivity in the maximal C-star-tensor product; for amenable groups, strict positivity in the minimal tensor product suffices.

title: Lie Hermitian manifolds with constant mixed curvature
abstract: We study Tang's conjecture on compact Hermitian manifolds. We prove that this conjecture holds for two special classes of unimodular Lie groups: their associated Lie algebras are either almost abelian, or contain a J-invariant abelian ideal of codimension two.

title: Polynomial complexity, random graphs, and strict ergodicity
abstract:
We construct infinite words $w$ whose complexity functions are quadratically bounded, but whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, resolving a question of Cassaigne.
  Moreover, we construct infinite words of polynomially bounded complexity, and subshifts of quasi-linear complexity, whose discrete derivatives do not decay compared to their complexity functions, thus exhibiting a typical exponentially-growing behavior. As an application, we give the first examples of subshifts of polynomial complexity whose Rauzy graphs do not have Benjamini-Schramm limits.
  Finally, we realize (up to an inevitable linear error factor) every function satisfying the necessary conditions, as the complexity function of a minimal, uniquely ergodic, cube-free subshift, strengthening previous realization results in this direction, and derive consequences for the growth of simple algebras and just-infinite semigroups satisfying nontrivial laws.

title: Generalized Edge Ideals and Regularity Offset of Graphs
abstract: We introduce generalized edge ideals by assigning pairwise coprime monomials, instead of variables, to the vertices of a graph. We use the lcm-lattice to show that the multigraded Betti numbers and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the quotient by a generalized edge ideal agree with the Betti numbers and resolution regularity of the quotient by an ordinary edge ideal in a non-standard Z-grading. We define the regularity offset as a measurement of the difference between the regularities of the quotients by a generalized edge ideal and its ordinary counterpart, and prove bounds for the regularity offset. We compute the regularity offset for co-chordal graphs and paths, and derive a formula for the regularity offset of forests. We also derive a graph-theoretic criterion for when a forest's regularity offset is always zero, or equivalently, its top-level Betti number is nonzero.

title: On nonlocal geometric rigidity estimates in bounded uniform domains
abstract: We prove fractional geometric rigidity estimates and fractional Korn's first inequalities with general singular weights in bounded uniform domains in $\mathbb R^n.$ The classical choice of the energy well $SO(n)$ for the geometric rigidity estimate fails due to the lack of a notion of orientation for Lebesgue fields. The remedy is to choose $O(n)$ as the energy well. Due to the recently developed theory of local-to-nonlocal passage of rigidity estimates developed by the first author, both estimates reduce to the analogous local estimates on the cube, which we prove in several steps by compactness and linearization arguments.

title: Plus Constructions and Canonical Induction for Green Categories
abstract: We develop canonical induction for Green categories associated with Mackey systems. We establish a change-of-rings framework in which the lower-plus and upper-plus constructions are realized by induction and coinduction of modules. The two plus adjunctions yield the mark morphism, and, when the relevant group orders are invertible in the coefficient ring, Möbius inversion gives an explicit inverse. Using the resulting linearization and tom Dieck maps, we construct a canonical induction map, give an explicit formula for it, and characterize when it is a right inverse of linearization. In the classical setting of Mackey functors, our construction and splitting criterion recover Boltje's results.

title: Reflexive polytopes can have doubly exponentially many vertices
abstract: Reflexive polytopes are lattice polytopes containing the origin in their interior such that also the dual polytope is a lattice polytope. On the basis of low-dimensional observations and of bounds known for special classes of reflexive polytopes, the second author conjectured in 2004 that the number of vertices of $d$-dimensional reflexive polytopes is bounded from above by $6^{d/2}$. In this note, we present counterexamples showing that this conjecture is false in every dimension $d \ge 8$. In fact, rather surprisingly, in sufficiently large dimensions $d$ the number of vertices (equivalently, by duality, the number of facets) can be as large as theoretically possible, namely doubly exponential in $d$. These results were found using GPT-6.1 Sol.

title: Multilevel kernel approximation of log-Euclidean manifold-valued functions
abstract: We study kernel approximation and multilevel residual correction for functions with values in a manifold that admits a global logarithm onto a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, such as positive definite matrices, exponential Lie groups, and Hadamard manifolds. Approximating in logarithmic coordinates keeps the approximant on the manifold and transfers Hilbert-space error estimates verbatim. To express these errors in the natural geometry of the target, we prove metric comparisons. In particular, we obtain a sharp, scale-invariant bound between the log-Euclidean and affine-invariant distances on positive definite matrices, with a constant that depends only on condition numbers. For multilevel approximation, compactly supported kernels scaled to the fill distance give algebraic convergence with sparse, uniformly well-conditioned systems. These guarantees require appropriate sample locations and approximation scales. Compact groups are treated through a principal logarithm, where a bi-invariant metric gives error bounds with constant one. Finally, the log-Euclidean and Karcher means differ by $\mathcal O(r^3)$ near the identity and by $\mathcal O(r^2)$ around a general point, where $r$ is the logarithmic data radius and the second bound is sharp.

title: Galois lines for the maximal curve with the second largest genus in characteristic two
abstract: We determine all Galois lines for the embedding of the maximal curve with the second largest genus in characteristic two into $\mathbb{P}^{3}$ induced by its Frobenius linear series. We also determine the associated Galois groups.

title: Sensing-Based Communication: A Non-Orthogonal Passive Reflection Framework for ISAC
abstract: While integrating uplink without disrupting the primary downlink remains a critical challenge for existing reflective communication systems, this paper proposes a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) mechanism termed Sensing-based Communication. Originating from and validated within an optical retro-reflective system, this mechanism possesses an underlying wave-agnostic architecture with the potential to be generalized across other physical modalities. It leverages incident downlink signals for parasitic modulation via passive tags. By relying solely on fundamental on-off keying (OOK) reflection, the tag unifies the reflective sensing channel and the uplink communication channel, and simultaneously achieves both sensing and duplex communication. Consequently, our approach introduces uplink capability without sacrificing the downlink data rate or consuming additional spectrum resources. At the receiver, we design a joint decoding architecture combining cross-correlation computation and successive interference cancelation (SIC) to fully exploit the degrees of freedom in broadband signals for multi-user interference suppression. We derive closed-form expressions for the interference and bit error rate (BER) assuming zero-mean Gaussian signals. Using an experimental testbed, we validate the pivotal theoretical finding, the scaling relationship of SINR with signal bandwidth and cross-correlation time--where linear regression yields a strong goodness-of-fit with $R^2 = 0.9688$. Furthermore, evaluations under noise-like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms exhibit high consistency between theoretical derivations and simulation data ($R^2 = 0.9372$, mean absolute percentage error, $\text{MAPE} = 14\%$), confirming the model's accuracy and waveform generalizability.

title: Exact optimality of augmented order-of-addition designs
abstract: We prove that, for the pairwise-ordering model with at least three components, adding any run to an order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a $D$-optimal design among all exact designs of the enlarged size, allowing replication. We also establish the corresponding result for foldover designs: adding any reversal pair to a foldover order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a $D$-optimal design within the foldover class at the enlarged size. Both augmentations also minimise the average prediction variance and a covariance-scaled information discrepancy, and maximise the minimum relative efficiency. The key step represents the scaled discrepancy through signed comparisons of triples and derives a sharp integer lower bound; classical spectral inequalities then give the exact-size optima, and signed four-component relative-order counts characterise equality. Complete reversal pairs additionally protect the estimation of pairwise-ordering effects against arbitrary reversal-invariant nuisance means. At the smallest estimable five-component foldover size, exact enumeration identifies five determinant-optimal classes with different prediction and balance properties, and a seven-component example shows that deleting a reversal pair need not be optimal even when it minimises the discrepancy. Constructions through ten components illustrate the attained run sizes.

title: Uniform and Relative Non-Associativity on Minimal Free Resolutions
abstract: We study unital chain-map multiplications on minimal free resolutions of quotient rings. We prove that Katthän's example admits no associative multiplication over any field, without assuming graded commutativity or compatibility with an internal grading. The proof gives a relative obstruction in which associativity on a specified finite collection of triples forces failure at another triple. The argument extends to a family that includes nonmonomial ideals. We also give criteria for uniform non-associativity, where a fixed triple fails for every multiplication, by comparing either associators or their primitives under changes of multiplication. These criteria persist from monomial elimination ideals and give explicit obstructions for Avramov's example and the known eight-vertex Bier sphere over every field. As an application, we show that the edge ideal of the eight-cycle admits an injective Taylor comparison on five selected generators, while every selection of that size fails to admit a multiplicative comparison. Four generators admit a multiplicative embedding.

title: Finite-rank Toeplitz commutators on the harmonic Bergman space
abstract: We completely characterize finite-rank commutators of Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk. Apart from affine dependence, finite rank occurs precisely when both symbols are analytic with rational primitives, or both are coanalytic and their complex conjugates have rational primitives. Our approach combines a block-matrix decomposition with Luecking's theorem, which rules out nonzero finite-rank Toeplitz operators with bounded symbols on the Bergman space. In particular, every such finite-rank commutator has square zero.

title: The quaternionic reflection groups with imprimitive complexifications and the finite subgroups of GL(2,C)
abstract: We give a transparent development of the quaternionic reflection groups which have imprimitive complexifications, including a description of their reflections and the corresponding normal reflection subgroups. They are seen to be of rank one or rank two, and are obtained from minimal complex reflection groups by the addition of one quaternionic reflection and a complex scalar matrix of finite order. In the case of the rank two groups, we use our techniques to consider the broader question of what are the minimal irreducible subgroups of GL(2,C) with a given collineation group. This leads to a complete classification of the finite irreducible subgroups of GL(2,C) in terms of the minimal groups, with the groups giving rise to quaternionic reflection groups located within it.

title: Special line bundles on tetragonal curves
abstract: One can associate a pair of vector bundles $(E, F)$ on $\mathbb{P}^1$ to every tetragonal curve: $E$ is the Tschirnhausen bundle and $F$ records numerical data of the ideal for the curve under its relative canonical embedding. In this note, we show that a Hurwitz--Brill--Noether general tetragonal curve must have balanced $E$, $F$ bundles, and provide counterexamples for the converse when $g = 8$ or $g \geq 10$.

title: Conley index theory for asymptotically autonomous systems and UV-to-IR connections
abstract: Many non-equilibrium systems, such as expanding plasmas, evolve by equations that depend explicitly on time and interpolate between autonomous early-time (UV) and late-time (IR) limits. After time is compactified, fixed points lie on invariant boundary fibers, where the Conley index is one-sided and blind to the UV. For time dependence that admits a $C^1$ compactification, we reflect the extended phase space across these fibers. Both sheets of the double run from the UV to the IR, and the UV index reappears, suspended by one degree. Extending one sheet slightly beyond both fibers gives an explicit UV-to-IR transport map between the Conley indices of the limit systems, and its non-vanishing forces connecting solutions. If one block with a fixed strict entrance/exit decomposition serves every frozen system, this map is an isomorphism at every admissible rate. If the block also has nonzero relative homology, the isolated invariant sets of the two limits are connected at every rate. In the Gubser flow of Israel-Stewart theory, the separatrix between two classes of initial data is a transversal connection at every finite relaxation scale $c$, with splitting $Δ(c)\propto1/c$. In the Bjorken flow at the lowest moment truncation, we prove existence and uniqueness of the attractor solution without regularization. For the three-dimensional Gubser system we construct the global Morse decomposition. In the one-loop flow of the $(4+ε)$-dimensional $O(N)$ model with cubic anisotropy, a shift of $N$ through $N=4$ has vanishing transport map, but a driven connection and a nonzero connecting homomorphism detect it at every rate.

title: Local cohomology over Steenrod algebras
abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q = p^s$ elements. Let $S = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} S_n$ be a non-negatively graded commutative, Noetherian $\mathbb{F}_q$-algebra. Assume $S$ has a structure of an unstable Steenrod algebra. Let $M$ be a finitely generated graded unstable $S$-module. Let $I$ be a homogeneous ideal in $S$. We prove that for $i \geq 0$ the local cohomology modules $H^i_I(M)$ has a structure of a Cartan $S$-module. As application we give a direct and considerably simpler proof of D. Bourguiba and S. Zarati's generalization of Landweber-Stong conjecture. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for $S$ to have $S_r$-property of Serre in terms of Dickson polynomials.

title: An Explicit Equation for the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Character Variety of $\mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2$
abstract: Let $N$ denote the closed non-orientable surface of Euler characteristic $-1$, i.e. the connected sum of three real projective planes $N = \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2$, with fundamental group presented as $\langle A,B,C \mid A^2 B^2 C^2 = I \rangle$ via the standard symmetric cross-cap model. Building on the classical trace-coordinate methods of Fricke, Vogt, and Goldman for free groups, and on the qualitative study of representation varieties of non-orientable surfaces by Benyash-Krivets and Chernousov, we give an explicit affine equation for a dense open piece of the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ GIT character variety $X(N)$. We prove that the trace coordinates $a = \mathrm{tr}(A)$, $b = \mathrm{tr}(B)$, $c = \mathrm{tr}(C)$, $p = \mathrm{tr}(AB)$ satisfy the polynomial relation $c^2 = abp - a^2 - b^2 + 4$, that this hypersurface is smooth and irreducible, and that on the open locus $c \neq 0$ it is isomorphic to the image of $X(N)$ under the trace map, with the remaining trace coordinates $\mathrm{tr}(BC)$, $\mathrm{tr}(CA)$, $\mathrm{tr}(ABC)$ recovered as regular functions on this locus. We further identify the boundary locus $c = 0$ with representations satisfying the matrix identity $A^2 B^2 = -I$, and describe its representation-theoretic structure, while leaving a complete global classification along this locus as an open problem. All key trace identities are proved from Cayley-Hamilton first principles and independently checked numerically against explicit matrices.

title: The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields, II
abstract:
We prove that every number field of odd degree $n\geq 3$ and absolute discriminant $D$ has an integral defining polynomial whose coefficients are $O_n(D^{(n-1)/(2n-1)})$ in size. This strengthens, in odd-degree cases, the recently established bound of $O_n(D^{1/2})$ for all degrees $n$, which was conjectured in 1998 by Ruppert and is now known to be optimal in even degrees. More generally, we prove that this strengthened bound holds for all degree-$n$ fields having a real embedding and no subfield of index two. The proof makes use of the lattice shapes of the ring of integers and its trace dual, the inverse different.
  Assuming the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions, as recently announced by Cureton and Thorner, we obtain an exponent smaller than $1/2$ for every field with no index-two subfield, of any signature. In the case of primitive fields, we obtain the exponent $(n-1)/(2n)$. In particular, we prove that the optimal exponent for cubic fields is $1/3$.

title: Delaunay classification of positive singular solutions to the critical Lane--Emden system
abstract:
We classify positive classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system \begin{align*} \begin{cases}
  -Δu=v^p & ~~\text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\},\\
  -Δv=u^q &~~ \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}, \end{cases}
  \end{align*} with a nonremovable singularity at $0$ (i.e., $\lim_{x\to0}u(x)=\lim_{x\to0}v(x)=+\infty$), where $n\ge3$ and $p,q>0$ satisfy \[
  \frac1{p+1}+\frac1{q+1}=\frac{n-2}{n}. \] Without additional growth or integrability assumptions, we establish radial symmetry about the origin, strict radial decrease, and global two-sided power bounds for both components. Furthermore, every such solution can be written as \[
  u(x)=|x|^{-α}U(\log|x|),\qquad
  v(x)=|x|^{-β}V(\log|x|), \] where $α=\frac{n}{q+1}$, $β=\frac{n}{p+1}$, and $(U,V)$ is either the positive equilibrium $(A,B)=((\fracαβ)^{\fracα{2}}, (\fracαβ)^{\fracβ{2}})$ or a positive nonconstant periodic solution of the associated Emden--Fowler system. These periodic solutions form a Delaunay family: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,A)$, there is a unique profile pair, up to translation in $t=\log|x|$, with $\min_{\mathbb{R}}U=\varepsilon$. The Hamiltonian energy provides an alternative parameter, decreasing continuously and strictly from zero to the equilibrium energy as $\varepsilon$ increases from $0$ to $A$. The common least period of the two components tends to infinity as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and to the period of the linearized oscillation at $(A,B)$ as $\varepsilon\uparrow A$. The classification includes the case of a sublinear exponent.

title: Constrained Nested-Logit Pricing: An Exact Reformulation and Global Optimization Method
abstract: Sellers must price substitutable products while meeting operational requirements such as price limits and sales targets. Nested logit captures stronger substitution among similar products, but these requirements can undermine the structure used to solve unconstrained pricing problems. We develop an exact reformulation and a global optimization method for a fixed assortment with price bounds and weighted price caps. The key novelty is to concentrate the difficult interactions at the nest level while retaining convex optimization over individual products, without discretizing prices or approximating demand. This structure makes the number of nests, rather than products, govern the exponent in a conditional worst-case complexity bound. The method returns feasible prices together with a bound on how much profit could still be gained, allowing decision makers to assess solution quality even when computation stops early. Extensions cover purchase-probability bounds and price-order rules, with explicit accounts of their computational cost. In synthetic experiments, the method certifies solutions for assortments of up to 500 products with few nests. Projecting unconstrained prices onto the feasible set loses up to 32.60% of profit relative to direct constrained optimization, highlighting the value of jointly optimizing substitution and feasibility.

title: An Elementary Proof of the Binary Goldbach Conjecture
abstract: We establish the binary Goldbach conjecture which asserts that every even positive integer greater than four can be expressed as a sum of two odd primes. This goal is achieved by proving that the number of ordered Goldbach pairs that add up to $2n$ is an $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{n}{\ln^{2} n}\right)$ function. As an application, we provide a simpler verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture that was first established in [6,7].

title: The Schur products of some nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes
abstract: In recent years, the Schur products of linear codes have been extensively studied due to their favorable applications in cryptography. In this paper, we aim to study the parameters of the Schur products of some nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes. Let $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ be two narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes with designed distances $δ_{1}$ and $δ_{2}$, respectively, where $2\le δ_{1},δ_{2}\le n$. Let $\mathcal{C}_1\star\mathcal{C}_2$ be the Schur product of $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$. We present some necessary and sufficient conditions for $\mathcal{C}_1\star\mathcal{C}_2\ne\mathbb{F}_q^n$ by applying some constraints to $δ_{1}$ and $δ_{2}$. Furthermore, we determine the dimensions of these products and lower bounds on their minimum distance. Several linear codes with best known parameters are found.

title: Bounds on Negligible Thresholds in Group Cohomology
abstract: Let $F$ be a field, $K/F$ a field extension with $Γ_K:=\text{Gal}(K_\text{sep}/K)$, $G$ a finite group, $j:Γ_K\rightarrow G$ a continuous group homomorphism, and $M$ an abelian group. There is an induced map of profinite cohomology $j^*:H^n (G;M)\rightarrow H^n (K;M)=:H^n (Γ_K;M)$. An element $u\in H^n (G;M)$ is negligible over $F$ if $j^* (u)=0$ for all such $j$ and field extensions $K/F$. The subset of negligible elements forms a subgroup $H^n (G;M)_{\text{neg},F}\subseteq H^n (G;M)$. The negligible threshold $\text{nthres}^G_F (M)$ is the smallest $N\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 0}\cup\{\infty\}$ such that $H^n (G;M)_{\text{neg},F}=H^n (G;M)$ for all $n\geq N$. In this paper, we first establish some general bounds for negligible thresholds of arbitrary triples $(G,M,F)$ consisting of a finite group $G$, trivial $G$-module $M$, and field $F$. We then compute the negligible thresholds of an arbitrary group when $F$ is a field of characteristic $p$ and $M=\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z}$. Continuing in the characteristic $p$ setting, we compute these thresholds for $G$ a $p$-group and $M=\mathbb{Z}$, and we compute the thresholds for $G=\mathbb{Z}/\ell\mathbb{Z},M=\mathbb{Z}/s\mathbb{Z}$ for integers $s,\ell\in\mathbb{N}_{>1}$ satisfying certain number theoretic conditions. For fields containing sufficiently many roots of unity, we show that the negligible threshold of odd exponent finitely-generated trivial $G$-modules is finite. For $G$-modules of the form $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, $p$ an odd prime, we compute an explicit upper bound for the negligible threshold in terms of $p$ and $|G|$. We conclude by providing explicit computations of the negligible thresholds of elementary abelian $p$-groups with mod-$p$ coefficients, negligible thresholds of cyclic groups, and bounds on mod-$p$ negligible thresholds of general finite abelian $p$-groups.

title: Jaeger conjecture and Jaeger-Zhang conjecture
abstract:
We prove that every signed planar graph $\widehat G$ of negative girth at least $\ell\geq 3$ satisfies $χ_c(\widehat G)<\frac{2\ell}{\ell-2}$. As a consequence, for every integer $k\geq 1$, every planar graph $G$ of odd girth at least $4k+3$ satisfies $χ_c(G)<\frac{2k+1}{k}$ and hence admits a homomorphism to $C_{2k+1}$.
  Our proofs build on recent results of Jafari on circular flows. In particular, Jafari proved that every $(4k+2)$-edge-connected graph has circular flow number strictly less than $2+\frac{1}{k}$. We revisit his theorem, providing an alternative proof that emphasizes the underlying graph-theoretic ideas. We also extend the result to signed graphs and weaken the connectivity assumption by imposing a lower bound only on the size of negative cuts.
  The key step is a small-correction lemma associated with a distribution on spanning trees. A splitting argument first gives the required correction in an even-degree graph; doubling the edges removes the degree-parity assumption. Plane duality then gives the coloring theorem. We discuss tightness of bounds in the end.

title: An improved isodiametric inequality for convex surfaces
abstract: Alexandrov conjectured that every closed convex surface of area $A$ and intrinsic diameter $D$ satisfies $A/D^2\leqπ/2$. Using an averaging argument over the curvature measure, we prove that every closed convex surface satisfies $A/D^2\leq2π/3$, improving the best previously known bound.

title: Pruning free resolutions over a complete intersection
abstract: Given a free resolution $F_\bullet$ over a polynomial ring $R$ and a system of higher homotopies on it for a regular sequence $a_1,\dots,a_c$, we can use the Eisenbud-Shamash construction to build a free resolution over $\overline{R}=R/(a_1,\dots,a_c)$. We provide a combinatorial formula for the new system of higher homotopies on a pruned free resolution $F_{\bullet}^{\mathcal{M}}$ that corresponds to a pruning of the Eisenbud-Shamash resolution.

title: Vector Lyapunov functions for nonconvex constrained optimization
abstract: Nonconvex constrained optimization problems are commonly solved by a Newton method for necessary conditions (sequential linear/quadratic programming) or a barrier reformulation (interior-point methods). We present a vector Lyapunov analysis for Newton-type algorithms based on constraint violation and optimality of the primal solutions to a sequence of approximate optimization problems. We thus prove local stability and convergence by constructing a strict Lyapunov function for the primal solution.

title: Blow-Up and Life-Span for Nonlinear Hardy-Hénon Parabolic Equations
abstract: We consider the nonlinear Hardy-Hénon parabolic equation $ u_t=Δu+|x|^l|u|^αu,$ $t>0,$ $x\in\mathbb{R}^N$ or $x\in\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}$, with $N\ge1$, $l>-\min\{2,N\}$, $α>0$, with nonnegative initial datum $u_0$. We first establish new criteria for finite-time blow-up. We then derive optimal upper bounds for the life-span $T_{\max}(λ\varphi)$ of solutions arising from the initial datum $u_0=λ\varphi$. These estimates establish a precise dependence of $T_{\max}(λ\varphi)$ on both the initial profile $\varphi$ and the parameter $λ$ in the small and large-amplitude regimes.

title: Fractional Fefferman--Stein inequalities on infinite rooted $k$-ary trees
abstract:
We study weighted endpoint estimates for the centered fractional maximal operator on the infinite rooted $k$-ary tree, $T$. Our first result is a Fefferman--Stein type estimate \[ w\bigl(\{M_αf>λ\}\bigr) \lesssim_{α,s} \frac1λ\sum_{x\in T}|f(x)|M_{α,s}w(x), \qquad s>1, \] with a constant independent of the branching parameter $k$. Although the proof is inspired by the non-fractional argument of Ombrosi, Rivera-Ríos and Safe in \cite{ORRS}, the fractional normalization introduces a genuinely new scale interaction. At radius $r$, one must renormalize the function by $k^{rα}$ while keeping the dyadic cutoff at $k^r$; this leads to a new summation mechanism involving simultaneously $k^{rα}$ and $k^{r(1-α)}$.
  We then study sharpness and the geometry of admissible weights. We construct counterexamples showing that the estimate cannot in general be reduced to $s=1$ for any $0<α<1$. In the subcritical range $0<α<1/2$, we characterize power-type radial weights satisfying the natural fractional $A_1$ condition and prove that the failure persists after any fixed finite number of iterations of $M_α$. We also prove that $M_αw\lesssim w$ is necessary for the corresponding weighted weak type estimate but is not sufficient in the subcritical range. Finally, we identify a phase transition: for $1/2\leα<1$ no nonzero global weight can satisfy $M_αw\lesssim w$.

title: Regularity of elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure
abstract: We study autonomous elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure of the form \[ -\operatorname{div}\big(\mathfrak a(|Du|)Du\big)=0 \quad \text{in }\ Ω\subset \mathbb R^n \] Under two-sided quantitative $(p,q)$-growth conditions on $\mathfrak a$, we prove gradient Hölder continuity with constants and exponent depending only on the dimensions, $p$ and $q$. This improves the classical theory initiated by Uhlenbeck by removing the continuity requirement on $\mathfrak a'$. The proof uses nonlinear comparison systems whose regularity follows from a scalar uniformly elliptic equation. Under weaker $(p,q)$-growth conditions on the convex function $\varphi(t):=\int_0^t s\mathfrak a(s)\,ds$, we obtain local $W^{1,s}$-regularity for every $s>1$, and hence Hölder continuity of solutions with every exponent less than one. An additional lower growth condition on $\mathfrak a$ yields local Lipschitz continuity, even when $\mathfrak a$ is discontinuous.

title: Singularities and Collision Criteria in the Gravitational Straight-Segment Problem with Arbitrary Positive Density
abstract: We study singularities and collision criteria for a massless particle around a fixed finite straight segment with an arbitrary positive continuous density. We first show that every singularity forces the trajectory to approach the material segment. Using the axial symmetry of the potential, we prove that any trajectory approaching the segment is confined to an invariant plane containing it. Moreover, we show that every singularity is either a collision singularity or an ejection singularity. Finally, in the invariant plane, we introduce an angular-cone condition for positions and momenta directed toward the segment. We prove that if the initial position-momentum pair belongs to the angular cone, then the trajectory collides with the segment in finite time, and we derive an upper bound for the collision time. We further prove that the final arc of any collision satisfies the angular-cone condition.

title: The Gibbons--Penrose inequality in Minkowski spacetime
abstract: We prove the Gibbons--Penrose inequality for smooth closed spacelike codimension-two submanifolds of Minkowski spacetime whose past null second fundamental form is non-negative. The proof is motivated by the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci technique.

title: Upper bound on the size of subgraphs avoiding cycles of girth length in graphs
abstract: A graph $G$ is said to be $H$-free if it contains no copy of $H$. The generalized Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$, a natural extension of the classical Turán number, is defined as the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. Although $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$ has been extensively studied for various specific graphs $G$, such as hypercubes, complete transposition graphs, and doubled Johnson graphs, very few results are known for general graphs. For a graph $G$ of girth $g$, let $C_{g}$ denote the cycle of length $g$. In this paper, we investigate the generalized Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(G, C_{g})$ for graphs $G$ in which every edge is contained in a fixed number of $g$-cycles, and establish a general upper bound on it. This bound generalizes the classical results on hypercubes and provides a unified approach for general graphs. Furthermore, we apply this bound to derive explicit upper bounds for several specific graphs, including $K_{n,n,\ldots,n}$, $K_{n}\times K_{n}$, $C_{m}\times C_{n}$, $S_{n}$, $AG_{n}$, $CT_{n}$ and $J(n;k,k+1)$.

title: Pósa-type resilience for Hamilton Berge cycles in random hypergraphs
abstract:
We prove a degree-sequence resilience theorem for Hamilton Berge cycles in random uniform hypergraphs. For every fixed integer $k\ge3$ and every $γ>0$, there exists $C=C(k,γ)>0$ such that if $C\log n/n^{k-1}\le p\le1$, then asymptotically almost surely every spanning subhypergraph of $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with increasing vertex-degree sequence $g_1\le\cdots\le g_n$ satisfying
  \[
  g_i\ge\left(\left(\frac{i}{n}\right)^{k-1}+γ\right)
  \binom{n-1}{k-1}p
  \qquad(1\le i<n/2)
  \]
  contains a Hamilton Berge cycle.
  The term $(i/n)^{k-1}$ agrees with the normalized asymptotic degree bound in Salia's deterministic Pósa-type theorem. Our result gives a hypergraph analogue of the random-graph theorem of Condon et al. and strengthens the sharp Dirac-type resilience theorem of Chen and Zhang at the same logarithmic probability order. The deletion-resilience formulation has optimal probability order up to constant factors. The coefficient $1$ of $(i/n)^{k-1}$ cannot be replaced by a smaller constant. The proof controls adaptive rotations and representative-edge incidences uniformly. It also gives an endpoint-growth estimate under nonuniform deletion bounds.

title: Disjointness preserving operators on Köthe-Banach spaces
abstract:
A well-known result of Abramovich says that if $E$, $F$ are rearrangement invariant Banach spaces on a finite atomless measure space such that $E$ has an absolutely continuous norm and $E\not\subseteq F$, then there are no nonzero disjointness preserving bounded linear operators $T \colon E\to F$.
  We obtain an analogue of this result in the setting of general Köthe-Banach spaces. Specifically, we identify a sufficient condition on Köthe-Banach spaces $E$, $F$ on finite atomless measure spaces that implies that there are no nonzero disjointness preserving bounded linear operators $T \colon E\to F$. Consequently, by a representation theorem for regular operators due to O.~Maslyuchenko, Mykhaylyuk and the second named author, this condition implies that every regular linear operator $T \colon E\to F$ is narrow. As an application, we obtain that if $1\le \max\{p_1,p_2\}< \min\{ r_1, r_2\}\le \infty$, then every regular linear operator $T \colon L_{p_1}(L_{p_2}) \to L_{r_1}(L_{r_2})$
  is narrow. The latter may be seen as an analogue of the classical Pitt compactness theorem.

title: Optimal domains of Volterra-type operators on Bergman spaces
abstract: We consider bounded Volterra-type operators $T_g$ from the weighted Bergman space $A^q_β$ to $A^p_α$. The holomorphic optimal domain $[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is introduced and shown to be a quasi-Banach space. We show that the intersection of the optimal domains is equal to $A^q_β$ if $p\le q$, while if $p>q$, it is strictly larger than $A^q_β$. Moreover, $A^q_β \subsetneq[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is established for $p\neq q$. If $p=q$, by contrast, $A^p_β$ may coincide with $[T_{g},A^p_α]$. The multiplier algebras and strict inclusions with respect to varying parameters are established. For example, we determine exactly when $[T_{g},A^s_γ] \subset [T_{g},A^p_α]$ for some $g\in \operatorname{Hol}(\mathbb{D})$. We further study the set $V_g^p$ and characterize the coincidence of the holomorphic optimal domains.

title: A Stone-Weierstrass Theorem for Polish Spaces, Given by Logic
abstract: The Stone-Weierstrass theorem obtains every continuous function on a compact space as a uniform limit of functions built from a separating family by finitely many operations, and Reggio proved the theorem equivalent to the Beth definability property of an infinitary equational logic. We extend both results beyond compactness: on every separable metric space, and in particular on every Polish space, every bounded uniformly continuous function is a uniform limit of functions built from countably many bounded separating functions by the connectives of infinitary real-valued logic, and an approximate Beth property of this logic is equivalent to the new theorem. The extension rests on a rule of syntax, which admits a countable supremum when its terms share an a priori bound and thereby makes the sentences define exactly the bounded Lipschitz functions, and on a model existence game that does the work of compactness in the proof of interpolation.

title: Reflections of Nichols algebras in braided monoidal categories
abstract: Let $\C$ be an essentially small abelian rigid braided monoidal category. We prove a reflection theorem for Nichols algebras in $\Ind(\C)$ and show that tuples admitting all reflections define connected semi-Cartan graphs. As applications, we prove that a finite Nichols algebra has a generating object of length at most one in $PSU(2)_k$ for odd $k\ge3$, in $SU(2)_{4m}$ for $m\ge1$, and in the representation categories of the Virasoro minimal models $\mathcal M(2,p)$ for odd $p\ge5$. In all three families, we prove that every finite pre-Nichols algebra is a Nichols algebra.

title: Slice Regular Capacity and Rational Approximation
abstract: Approximation theory in the complex plane is a well established area of mathematical research, with extensive contributions documented in the literature, notably through the classical results of Weierstrass, Runge, Mergelyan, and Vitushkin. Approximation theory in quaternionic settings, particularly rational approximation on compact sets, which studies when slice regular functions can be uniformly approximated by rational functions, is one of the recent areas of interest in quaternionic rational approximation theory (See [6,13]). In this paper, we discuss Vitushkin approximation theorem in the quaternionic setting by using the quaternionic analogue of analytic capacity and also we establish Davies modified Vitushkin scheme in quaternionic setting. We also discuss quaternionic analogue of $γ_{+}$- capacity and Cauchy capacity and the remarkable results of Tolsa [35] and Younsi [45] related to these capacities in complex plane setting.

title: A counterexample to Manin's Conjecture for almost Fano varieties
abstract: We give an example of a smooth rational threefold over a number field with a big anticanonical divisor that does not satisfy the thin set version of Manin's Conjecture. In particular, Manin's Conjecture does not hold for rationally connected almost Fano varieties.

title: KAM theory for quasi-periodic equilibrium of generalized Frenkel-Kontorova model in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$
abstract: We extend the KAM theory for one dimensional Frenkel-Kontorova model to multidimensional case in quasi-periodic media. By using the quasi-Newton method, we reduce the linearized operator with quasi-periodic coefficient in the Nash-Moser iteration to the composition of two diagonal operators and a near-identity operator, such that the small divisor problem can be overcome by imposing the simultaneous Diophantine condition. In contrast, we also discuss the application of Craig-Wayne-Bourgain method to the quasi-periodic equilibrium problem.

title: Local contraction of stochastic affine recursions of $\mathbb{R}^d$
abstract: We consider affine stochastic recursions $X^x_{n+1}=A_{n+1}X^x_n+B_{n+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $(B_n,A_n)$ are i.i.d. in $\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with strongly irreducible and proximal linear part. In the critical regime where the top Lyapunov exponent vanishes, we show that the recursion is locally contractive in every direction, yielding uniqueness, up to a positive multiplicative constant, of the $μ$-invariant non-zero Radon measure. This extends to every dimension $d\geq 2$ a result of Babillot-Bougerol-Élie (1997) in dimension one. The proof is based on the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the "joint process" $(X^x_n,X^y_n)$, using geometric and measure-theoretic properties of the diagonal affine action. A key ingredient is an abstract criterion for the total dissipativity of semigroup actions, which we apply to this process.

title: Global regularity of the two-dimensional fractional Boussinesq equations with critical dissipation
abstract: In the present paper, our primary focus is on the Boussinesq equations with fractional velocity dissipation $Λ^αu$ and temperature diffusion $Λ^βθ$. On the critical balance line $α+β=1$, establishing global regularity for weak velocity dissipation has been obstructed by the quadratic convective-buoyancy feedback, and all available results below $α=\frac{10}{13}$ require a smallness assumption on the initial temperature. In this paper, we prove large-data global regularity across the extended regime $α>\frac{\sqrt{57}-5}{4} \approx 0.637$. This provides a step beyond the previous barrier $α=\frac{10}{13}$, unconditionally dismantling the temperature smallness assumption that has persisted in the literature for over a decade. The mathematical mechanism relies on a high-order Quadratic Normal Form transformation $H=ω-R_αθ-\Bop(θ,θ)$ tailored to eliminate non-resonant quadratic vorticity-temperature interactions. Crucially, by uncovering the exact physical scalings of the underlying multilinear commutators and maintaining sharp fractional conjugates in the $L^m$-energy framework, we ensure that the global energy closure is governed entirely by the quadratic thermal dissipation. Once an integrability threshold $m>\frac{2}α$ is attained, a fine Littlewood-Paley transport estimate drives a fractional regularity gain $H \in B_{r,\infty}^{3α-2}$, ensuring the velocity field achieves critical drift regularity $C^α$. By Silvestre-type drift regularization, this spontaneously generates positive Hölder continuity for the temperature, which in turn elevates the drift regularity strictly beyond the critical threshold, unlocking non-local Schauder estimates to prevent finite-time singularity formation.

title: Multi-monopoles and monodromy around the wobbly divisor
abstract: The multi-monopole equations are a generalisation of the Seiberg--Witten equations where the spinor is coupled to an auxiliary vector bundle. The signed count of multi-monopoles on a 3-manifold can vary according to a new type of wall-crossing phenomenon. For products $S^1\times C$, where $C$ is a closed Riemann surface, we relate the wall and chamber structure to loops in the complement of the wobbly divisor of $C$. Such a loop induces a monodromy map on the multi-vortex moduli space, and the count of its fixed points is expected to agree with the count of multi-monopoles on $S^1\times C$ in the given chamber. By studying singularities of framed multi-vortex moduli spaces, we are able to understand these monodromy maps for various loops. Counting fixed points suggests that product 3-manifolds display incredibly rich wall-crossing behaviour.

title: Entropic Martingale Optimal Transport with Wasserstein Relaxed Marginal Constraints
abstract: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) is a fundamental framework in robust finance, yet its stability under marginal perturbation no longer holds in high dimensions $d\geq 2$. In this paper, we introduce Wasserstein-relaxed entropic martingale optimal transport (WEMOT), which combines Wasserstein relaxation of the second marginal with entropy regularization. This formulation ensures stability under perturbations of the marginals, thereby facilitating numerical implementation. We establish strong duality and dual attainment for WEMOT, which leads to efficient Sinkhorn-type algorithms. We further prove a convergence rate of WEMOT to MOT as regularization parameters vanish, and also the quantitative stability of WEMOT with respect to marginal perturbations.

title: Infinitely many convex polytopes with dihedral angles bounded above by $π/2+δ$
abstract: For every $δ>0$, we construct infinitely many pairwise combinatorially distinct convex three-dimensional polytopes whose dihedral angles are all less than $π/2+δ$.

title: Critical Resonance and the Radial Branch in Maz'ya's Weighted Hessian--Gradient Inequality
abstract:
We study the sharp constant $C(p,γ)$ in Maz'ya's planar weighted inequality \[
  \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|\nablaψ|^p|x|^{p(γ-1)}\, \mathrm{d} x
  \le C(p,γ)\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|D^2ψ|_{\mathrm{F}}^p|x|^{pγ}\, \mathrm{d} x, \] where $|\cdot|_{\mathrm{F}}$ denotes the Frobenius norm. For every fixed $1\le p<\infty$, with $a=γ-1+2/p$, we prove \[
  C(p,γ)^{-1}=2^{p/2}|a|^p+O_p(|a|^{p+1})\qquad(a\to0). \] The leading term comes from the first angular harmonics after the Emden--Fowler transform. We also determine explicit exterior parameter rays on which the unrestricted constant equals the radial value $(1+a^2)^{-p/2}$. The proof uses an entropy identity and a homogeneous calibration. In the remaining transition region, we obtain symmetry-breaking intervals and a necessary and sufficient condition for nonnegativity of the periodic second variation at the radial state. An explicit example shows that global symmetry breaking can occur even when this second variation is nonnegative.

title: A Trivalent Graph of Girth 14 and Order 372
abstract: The smallest known trivalent graph of girth 14 is constructed. The graph has 372 vertices, improving the old upper bound of 384 \cite{exoo14}. The construction uses methods that may be new to this problem.

title: Power Mean, Karcher Mean, and Log-Euclidean Mean on Positive Constant Upper Triangular Matrices
abstract: We study weighted power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means on the Lie group CP_n of real upper triangular matrices with a constant positive diagonal. Building on the general triangular-group theory, we use the central decomposition CP_n \cong \mathbb R_+ -by-UP_n to separate the scalar power mean from a unipotent mean with reweighted coefficients. We prove that the power mean extends real-analytically through order zero, where it equals the Karcher mean. We establish exterior-power covariance for the Karcher and log-Euclidean means, and tensor-product identities for all three means, distinguishing product weights from paired inputs. Finite nilpotent functional calculus yields concise formulas on CP_2 and CP_3, where the Karcher and log-Euclidean means coincide. In dimension four, their difference is exactly a central cubic commutator, giving a necessary and sufficient equality criterion and an explicit counterexample. In every dimension, the same commutator is the leading term of their small-dispersion difference.

title: Burgess' bounds with prime moduli
abstract: Let $S_χ(N)= \sum_{n\leq N} χ(n)$, where $χ$ is a Dirichlet character modulo a prime $p$. For integral $r\geq 2$, Burgess gave bounds of the shape $S_χ(N) \ll N^{1-1/r} p^{(r+1)/(4r^{2})} \log p$. The factor of $\log p$ was reduced by several authors. We show that it can be removed completely.

title: Standard Subspaces and Modular Theory -- General Theory and Applications to QFT
abstract: This is a preview of an upcoming monograph on standard subspaces and modular theory. At the moment, it consists of the first chapter. This starts with a gentle introduction to the subject, and then describes the modular theory of standard subspaces, the characterization of their modular data by the KMS condition and reflection positivity, and various constructions of standard subspaces. Further topics in Chapter 1 include the connection of standard subspaces to complexifications and symplectic structures, including their polarizers, and operations with standard subspaces, namely direct sums, direct integrals, and tensor products. Many examples and classification results are included as well. This first chapter also contains a description of the free U(1)-current and some other applications to quantum field theory, such as KMS states of type I factors, the local subspaces of the free Klein--Gordon field, and the entropy operator defined by a standard subspace.

title: The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
abstract: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio $μ\to 0$. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.

title: Twisted Verlinde Formula for Finite Cyclic Orbifolds of Vertex Operator Algebras
abstract: Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite and self-dual vertex operator algebra of CFT type, and let $G$ be a finite cyclic automorphism group of $V$. We establish a twisted Verlinde formula for cyclic groups of arbitrary finite order, expressing fusion coefficients among twisted $V$-modules in terms of the $S$-matrix in the orbifold theory. As an application, we compute fusion rules among twisted modules for the permutation orbifold $\left(V^{\otimes k}\right)^{\langle g\rangle}$ associated with a $k$-cycle $g=(1\,2\,\cdots\,k)$.

title: The splitting type of jet bundles on the projective line
abstract: Given a vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on a smooth variety X, one can associate to it its jet bundles, or bundles of principal parts. These bundles encode the Taylor expansions of local sections of $\mathcal{E}$ and arise naturally in the study of differential operators. When $X=\mathbb{P}^1$ is the projective line, jet bundles decompose as direct sums of line bundles, making it natural to study their splitting types. The splitting type is well understood in characteristic zero, but exhibits subtler behavior in positive characteristic. Our goal is to give a complete answer in every positive characteristic, and in particular to provide a characterization of semistability for jet bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$. We also determine their extremal summands and give applications to differential operators and formulas for cohomology of line bundles on infinitesimal thickenings of the diagonal.

title: Long-root $\SL_2$ dual pairs in split exceptional groups: Compact types, cone geometry, and theta correspondence
abstract: The paper establishes a case of Howe duality for an exceptional theta correspondence using the ping-pong of types method. To that end, one needs to compute lifts of types of maximal compact subgroups. A brand new ingredient enters here: The graded module of the minimal representations is the coordinate ring of an affine cone whose projectivization is a Grassmannian. Via the filtered Nakayama lemma the problem of lifting types becomes a problem in algebraic geometry: compute certain linear sections of the Grassmannian.

title: Stability of large dynamical systems using Gershgorin Disc Theorem
abstract: Understanding the stability of large nonlinear dynamical systems is a fundamental problem in many fields, including biological, technological, and social networks. Traditional stability methods often rely on explicit eigenvalue calculations or the construction of Lyapunov functions, which become computationally difficult for large interconnected systems. In this work, we introduce a stability classifier that provides a computationally efficient way to determine the stability of complex systems without performing full spectral analysis. Our approach combines the Dynamical Jacobian Ensemble framework, which uses the network structure and the underlying dynamics to construct a Jacobian, with the Gershgorin disc theorem, which provides bounds on the eigenvalues of the system's Jacobian matrix. Using this combination, we derive an analytical classifier that predicts whether a dynamical system is asymptotically stable, unstable, or sensitively stable based on a small set of dynamical and network parameters. The analysis reveals that the stability of large dynamical systems is strongly influenced by highly connected hub nodes. This observation allows the stability condition to be simplified by focusing on the contribution of the hub-associated Gershgorin disc. Extensive numerical simulations on large ensembles of Jacobian matrices confirm that the proposed classifier accurately separates stable, unstable, and sensitively stable regimes across a wide range of dynamical parameters and network structures. The resulting framework provides a simple and scalable tool for predicting the stability of large dynamical networks while capturing the interplay between network topology and interaction dynamics.

title: Counting Finite Maps through Functional Digraphs and Fibers
abstract: We count solutions of composition identities for maps on finite sets, first for three identities in which both maps vary and then for commutation with a prescribed arithmetic map. For $f\circ g=f\circ g\circ g$, drawing an arrow from each element to its image reduces the enumeration to rooted trees attached to directed cycles. For $f\circ f=f\circ g\circ f$, grouping elements with the same $f$-value leads instead to a partition-based enumeration. A classical rooted-forest enumeration leads in both problems to $\mathcal T(x)$, the exponential generating function for rooted labeled trees. For $f=g\circ f\circ g$, the values on the cycles of $g$ determine all remaining values. The exponential generating function $\mathcal D$ for these ordered pairs and the ordinary generating function $\mathcal A$ for endofunctions up to relabeling satisfy $\mathcal D(x)=\mathcal A(\mathcal T(x))$. Finally, we count functions on $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ satisfying $f(ax)=af(x)$, first for prime multipliers $a$ and then for a broader class of composite multipliers. In each problem, fixing one map exposes independent choices for the other through its functional digraph or its fibers.

title: Liouville transforms for ordinary differential equations with distributional coefficients
abstract: We study Liouville transforms for the differential equation $Ju'+qu=wf$ on the real interval $(a,b)$ where $J$ is a constant, invertible, skew-hermitian matrix and $q$ and $w$ are matrices whose entries are distributions of order $0$ with $q$ Hermitian and $w$ non-negative. In particular, we examine their use in the treatment of quasi-regular endpoints and their impact on the Weyl-Titchmarsh $\mathbb M$-function associated with the differential equation.

title: How the $p$-Bergman metric approaches the Carathéodory metric
abstract: We study the rate at which the $p$-Bergman metric approaches the Carathéodory metric on convex domains with measures comparable to $δ^αdV$, $α>-1$. On smooth convex domains of finite type the logarithmic coefficient is bounded above by the harmonic-measure average of the tangential multitype dimension plus $1+α$, with equality when almost every endpoint of the extremal disc is coercive. For a class of convex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with $C^4$ boundary and rank-one real tangential contact along an axis disc, a winding number distinguishes the coefficient $2+α$ from an upper bound $7/4+α$; quartic contact makes the latter bound exact. The exact value holds along the entire axis of explicit real-algebraic strongly pseudoconvex domains, including perturbations without the weighted circle action, although their pointwise boundary models agree up to unitary equivalence with those of a domain having coefficient $2+α$. A $C^2$ example has negative winding but coefficient $2+α$, with a $-\frac12\log\log p$ correction, so boundary regularity is essential to the gap theorem.

title: Interacting Urn Schemes on Infinite Graphs: A Representation Approach
abstract: Interacting urn schemes have emerged as an important framework for studying reinforcement phenomena in interacting stochastic systems (see, e.g., \cite{launay2011interacting,launay2012generalized,WARM2014,aletti2017interacting,Synchronisation-2,kaur2023interacting,kaur2023interacting2}). Most existing results, however, are restricted to finite systems. In this article, we investigate interacting urn schemes involving infinitely many urns, where the interactions are naturally described by a directed graph. The reinforcement or drawing mechanism at each urn depends on the compositions of its in-neighboring urns. To analyze the asymptotic behavior of these systems, we develop a representation of the urn dynamics in terms of branching Markov processes evolving on a class of random forests introduced in this article. This extends the representation approach of \cite{bandyopadhyay2022new}, originally developed for single Pólya urn schemes, to interacting urn schemes on locally finite directed graphs. Using this representation, we establish almost sure convergence of the color proportions under standard conditions on the reinforcement matrix or kernel. In particular, we show that the convergence holds independently of the topology of the underlying graph, and hence our results also apply to undirected graphs, where the interactions are bidirectional. We further investigate measure-valued generalizations and other related reinforced stochastic processes, illustrating the broad applicability of the representation approach. Finally, we discuss connections with self-organized criticality.

title: Gaussian fluctuations of the moderately interacting Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto particle system around the mollified mean-field limit
abstract: We study, at the logarithmic mollification scale $η^{-2(d+1+α)}\leδ\log N$ of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{ü}ngel, the fluctuation field $V^N=\sqrt N(μ^N-u_η)$ of the moderately interacting multi-species particle system whose mean-field limit is the Shigesada- Kawasaki-Teramoto (SKT) cross-diffusion system. The field is centred at the solution $u_η$ of the mollified equation, which depends on $N$ through $η$. On a scale of weighted Bessel-potential spaces of negative order we prove that the laws of $(V^N,M^N)$ are tight, where $M^N$ is the martingale part. Every limit point of $M^N$ is a continuous Gaussian martingale with an explicit deterministic bracket. Every limit point of $V^N$ is a weak solution, and the mild solution, of a linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck SPDE whose drift is the linearisation of the SKT operator at the limit $u$. The initial field and the martingale are independent, and weak solutions are unique given both, so the whole sequence converges in law, jointly with the martingale part, and the limit is unique in law among solutions of the martingale problem. The noise is $d M_i=div(\sqrt{2u_iΘ_i}dW_i)$, with $Θ_i=σ_i+\sum_jf(a_{ij}u_j)$ and $W$ a cylindrical Wiener process on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^{nd})$. The hypotheses are those of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{ü}ngel, including the smallness and the nonnegativity on $\mathbb{R}$ of the nonlinearity $f$. We add radial kernels $B_{ij}$, the independence of the initial data and the Brownian motions across particles and species, a smaller $δ$, a regularity budget on $u_0$, a strengthened smallness condition on $f$ that makes the backward system diagonally dominant in weighted spaces, and an integer Sobolev index $s$.

title: Algorithms for Short Human-Verifiable Proofs of Non-Word-Representability
abstract:
A graph is word-representable if it can be represented using alternation of letters in words. The class of word-representable graphs generalizes several important graph families and admits a characterization via semi-transitive orientations. Recognizing word-representability is an NP-complete problem, and a major bottleneck in the theory of word-representable graphs is providing efficient justifications of non-word-representability of graphs, rather than merely referring to software verification.
  Recently, Kitaev and Sun initiated the development of methods for the automatic generation of human-verifiable proofs of non-word-representability. They introduced three algorithms and evaluated their performance on the 25 connected non-word-representable graphs on seven vertices, which constitute a fairly small sample set.
  In this paper, we confirm their ranking of the algorithms by testing them on all non-word-representable graphs on eight and nine vertices. We further introduce three new algorithms, one of which significantly outperforms the previously best method on graphs with at most nine vertices, producing substantially shorter proofs. We apply this algorithm to shorten a known proof of non-word-representability of the Shrikhande graph and to produce a proof of non-word-representability of a certain subgraph of the Kneser graph $K(8,3)$. This subgraph is the first known example of a triangle-free non-word-representable graph, presented in the literature with reference only to a computational proof. As a by-product of our study, we correct an error in the repeatedly published list of the 25 connected non-word-representable graphs on seven vertices.

title: Domain-uniform integration lower bounds and local information
abstract: We study deterministic numerical integration on open subsets of $\mathbb R^d$ of volume one. Let $e_n$ be the minimal worst-case error using at most $n$ function values. For twice continuously differentiable functions with the normalized Lipschitz bounds proposed by Novak, we prove $e_n\geq v_d^{-2/d}n^{-2/d}/(4(d+2))\geq(8π\mathrm e)^{-1}n^{-2/d}$, where $v_d$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball. This resolves Novak's conjecture: the lower-bound constant is independent of the dimension and the shape of the domain. A midpoint rule on the cube has the same rate, up to an absolute constant. The proof uses smooth functions that vanish near the sample points and are large elsewhere. The bound therefore remains valid when each sample supplies all local information about the function. For scalar linear targets continuous in the uniform norm, we prove a second result on the global smooth class with prescribed function, gradient, and Hessian bounds: adaptive local information has the same minimal error as values and gradients at points chosen in advance. We give extensions to function recovery, finite integration measures, and anisotropic derivative bounds.

title: Centralizers of elliptic univalent self-maps and the embeddability problem in the unit disc
abstract:
Let $φ$ be an elliptic univalent self-map of the unit disc in the complex plane that is not an automorphism, with multiplier $0<|λ|<1$ at its Denjoy--Wolff point. The simultaneous Schröder linearization of maps commuting with $φ$ is classical. Using this linearization, we identify its univalent centralizer with the multiplicative semigroup of scalars that preserve the Koenigs domain, and investigate how the geometry of this semigroup controls continuous-time embeddings.
  We show that the identity is a non-isolated point of the centralizer precisely when the centralizer contains a non-trivial continuous one-parameter semigroup; such a semigroup need not contain $φ$. For each logarithmic branch $μ_k=-\mathrm{Log}λ+2πi k$, we establish a local sector alternative that characterizes the existence of an embedding with spectral value $μ_k$.
  We prove that the set of admissible branch indices is either empty, a finite interval of integers, or all of $\mathbb{Z}$, and give examples realizing all three possibilities. Finally, we describe the full holomorphic centralizer, including the constant map with value equal to the Denjoy--Wolff point.

title: Reweighting for Transfer Classification: Exact Risk Conversion and Minimax Adaptation
abstract: A source can make a training mixture easier to learn while making its accuracy less valuable for the target. We study how the training problem a source creates and the finite-sample error of learning it jointly determine target-risk guarantees under reweighting. For binary classification, for each pair of laws and each positive target weight, we derive the sharpest target excess hinge-risk bound implied by mixture excess alone, uniformly over clipped predictors. This exact conversion curve is determined by density-weighted local votes. A two-sample oracle inequality for weighted support vector machines supplies the mixture excess, and the composition becomes explicit for Gaussian kernels.
