On a tilted-boundary class, we establish the all-procedure minimax classification rate $[n+s_+^2/(m^{-1}+τ^2)]^{-1}$ in the transferable strength $s_+$ and the tilt $τ$, separating source sampling uncertainty ($m^{-1}$) from relation uncertainty ($τ^2$). A target-checked Gaussian-SVM selector adapts to unknown $s_+$ and $τ$ up to a logarithmic factor for fixed dimension, and retains the target-only rate up to the same factor against arbitrary independent sources under the stated target model. On a separate smooth opposition class, the minimax risk within the family of exact Gaussian SVMs fitted to the original labels with nonnegative weights is exponentially larger than the unrestricted minimax risk whenever the target sample is at most half the source sample, despite arbitrary data-dependent weighting and tuning. The value of a source thus depends on the training problem it creates, on what accuracy there means for the target, and on whether the permitted use of the source can implement the needed correction.

title: A new characterization of the round sphere
abstract: We provide an elementary proof of Hersch's inequality and Cheng's theorem, both characterizing the sphere. We revisit these classical results in connection with the geodesic monotonicity of heat kernels on two-dimensional spheres, which provides a third characterization.

title: Projective flatness of cylindrically symmetric Finsler metrics
abstract: In this paper, we study cylindrically symmetric projectively flat Finsler metrics \(F=|\bar y|φ(x^0,r,s,z)\). We reformulate the conditions for projective flatness and strong convexity in terms of \(Ω=φ-sφ_s-zφ_z\), isolating the compatibility condition missing in earlier work. Using the method of characteristics, we give an integral formula for all smooth local solutions near points with \(r>0\) and \(s=z=0\). These solutions are determined by a characteristic potential up to the addition of an invariant exact one-form. In the reversible case, the equation for the potential reduces to a \((2+1)\)-dimensional wave equation on a half-space. We illustrate the reconstruction with a polynomial potential and compute the potentials of a known family of spherically symmetric metrics and their linear pullbacks. The convexity conditions also admit decreasing profiles and recover the spherical Beltrami metric as a particular case. Finally, suitable positive sums of linear pullbacks yield smooth reversible projectively flat Finsler metrics on \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) whose tangent norm at the origin is non-Riemannian. Consequently, these metrics are not linear pullbacks of spherically symmetric metrics

title: On the Volume Conjectures for Dehn-filled $3$-manifolds along fundamental shadow link complements with big volume
abstract: We prove the Volume Conjecture and the Asymptotic Expansion Conjecture for closed oriented hyperbolic $3$-manifolds obtained by integral Dehn-fillings along a fundamental shadow link complement, provided that their volumes are sufficiently close to that of the complement. More generally, we show that the conjectured asymptotic expansions hold for pairs obtained by change-of-pair operations on a fundamental shadow link complement whenever the volume of the corresponding hyperbolic cone manifold is sufficiently close to that of the complement. A key ingredient in the proof is the introduction of extended quantum $6j$-symbols and a Weak Reflection Symmetry satisfied by them. The Weak Reflection Symmetry is established by relating the extended quantum $6j$-symbols to the $b$-$6j$ symbols through a real Gevrey-$1$ estimate and a truncated Borel-Laplace transform.

title: Walsh Analysis in the Twenty-First Century: Convergence, Summability, Nonlinear Approximation, Universality, and Digital Applications
abstract: Walsh analysis connects ordered Fourier convergence, summability, nonlinear approximation, and universal representation through a common character algebra. This survey examines developments from 2000-2026 against their classical foundations. Binary kernel geometry explains Hardy-space losses and summability thresholds; interval and packet methods control spectral selection; localized blocks produce correction and universal representations with distinct coefficient and exceptional-set requirements. Selected proofs and counterexamples compare these mechanisms and identify where an implication needs an additional hypothesis. The same distinctions organize digital integration, sparse measurements, Boolean spectra, and generalized Walsh bases. Quantitative thresholds, source conventions, and published theorem pointers are collected in comparative tables. The concluding problems separate source-listed questions, proposed refinements, and elementary obstructions. Supplementary derivations preserve normalization checks and finite covariance calculations while keeping the main exposition focused on the analytic mechanisms.

title: Sharp condition for Superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation
abstract: We determine the sharp condition for local superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation $(-Δ)^m u=u^{(n+2m)/(n-2m)}$, where $m\geq2$ is an integer and $n>2m$. For a solution in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at zero, local superharmonicity holds if and only if $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)>0$. The threshold is sharp. In the biharmonic case $m=2$, for every $n\geq5$, we construct smooth positive solutions of $Δ^2u=u^{(n+4)/(n-4)}$ in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at $0$, satisfying $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)=0$ and $\limsup_{x\to0}u(x)=+\infty$, while $-Δu$ converges to a finite negative limit along a fixed ray. The construction relies on an infinite array of concentrating bubbles arranged on concentric polygons, with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction controlling their interactions against a vanishing background.

title: Extensions of operators between ordered vector spaces
abstract: We prove analogues of several classical theorems about operators between vector lattices in the context of directed Archimedean ordered vector spaces. In particular, we show that every order continuous operator between pervasive Archimedean ordered vector spaces can be extended to an order continuous operator between their Dedekind completions. Additionally, we introduce the universal completion of a directed Archimedean ordered vector space, and show that every supremum-preserving operator between directed Archimedean ordered vector spaces can be extended to an order continuous homomorphism between their universal completions. We also establish some universal properties for the relative uniform completion.

title: Optimal Feedback Control of the Fokker-Planck Equation for an SIRS Epidemic Model
abstract: We develop a Fokker--Planck feedback control framework for a stochastic susceptible--infected--recovered--susceptible (SIRS) epidemic model with three intervention mechanisms targeting disease transmission, loss of immunity, and recovery. The interventions are formulated as space- and time-dependent feedback controls that influence both the drift and diffusion coefficients of the underlying stochastic differential equations, allowing control of the probability distribution of epidemic states. We investigate the existence of optimal controls and derive first-order necessary optimality conditions involving a forward Fokker--Planck equation, a backward adjoint equation, and a Hamiltonian minimization condition. For numerical approximation, we combine a Chang--Cooper discretization of the diagonal drift--diffusion terms with a finite-difference treatment of cross-diffusion and a sequential quadratic Hamiltonian (SQH) algorithm for computing the optimal feedback policies. We also examine sufficient-decrease and convergence properties of the SQH iteration. Numerical experiments consider four epidemiological objectives involving cumulative infection burden, infection-threshold exceedance, terminal susceptible population, and a combination of running and terminal costs. The resulting feedback policies exhibit distinct spatial and temporal structures depending on the epidemiological objective. Monte Carlo simulations of the underlying stochastic system illustrate that the optimized interventions can substantially reduce infection growth and undesirable epidemic outcomes relative to uncontrolled dynamics. The proposed framework provides a distribution-based approach to stochastic epidemic control that integrates mathematical analysis, numerical optimization, and state-dependent intervention design.

title: McShane's identity and the Brownian loop measure
abstract: We combine McShane's identity for a once-punctured torus with the length-spectrum identity of Wang and Xue. An exact identity in each primitive homology class yields a finite limit for the difference of two divergent length-spectrum sums over self-intersecting hyperbolic geodesics. The limit is $\frac18$ and is equivalent to McShane's identity. We also derive higher-iteration identities governed by integer divisors.

title: Non-conical classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated singularity
abstract: Several examples of one-homogeneous classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated free boundary singularity are known. Adapting the approach of Caffarelli, Hardt, and Simon for minimal surfaces, we construct non-conical classical solutions with an isolated free boundary singularity by perturbing a one-homogeneous solution $U$. Moreover, if $U$ is strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate), then any solution sufficiently close to $U$ is also strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate).

title: Branch-Extended Automatic Differentiation
abstract: We present branch-extended automatic differentiation (BEAD), a software package that provides information about inactive branches of piecewise-differentiable functions, intended for use in nonsmooth optimization algorithms. BEAD is implemented in Python, building on the popular JAX framework. For supported nonsmooth operations such as abs and max, BEAD identifies alternative branches within tolerance from the given input, and computes gradients of the resulting branches extended to the given input. Such information has been previously used for robust optimization methods, but has required error-prone and tedious manual differentiation, unlike BEAD, which is fully automated for functions written in NumPy-like JAX code. Our experiments show that our approach is as accurate as manually written derivative code, and offers more flexibility in modifying the function and choosing between branch-discovery rules. While we were originally motivated by the manifold sampling algorithm for nonsmooth composite objectives, we also integrate BEAD branch-extension gradients into a nonsmooth BFGS-SQP solver. On two small nonsmooth test problems, the resulting path-aware search resolves failures or substantially reduces the number of evaluations required by the BFGS-SQP solver.

title: Nonzero solutions for Dirichlet problems with the competing (p,q)-Laplacian
abstract: The following equation is considered: $$-Δ_p u(\boldsymbol{x}) + Δ_q u(\boldsymbol{x}) = f\big(\boldsymbol{x}, u(\boldsymbol{x})\big)\text{ for } \boldsymbol{x} \in Ω, \qquad u(\boldsymbol{x}) = 0 \text{ for } \boldsymbol{x}\in \partial Ω.$$ We start by showing that the energy functional associated with the considered problem no longer has the properties typical of its non-competing counterpart, which prevents a direct application of standard variational and monotonicity methods. Using Ekeland's variational principle combined with properties imposed on the nonlinear term~$f$, we prove the existence of a nonzero generalized solution to the problem. It is also shown that in the one-dimensional case $Ω= (-1,1)$, assuming that $f$ satisfies the symmetry conditions $$f(x,u) = f(-x,u) = -f(x,-u),$$ together with the sign condition $f(x,u) \geq 0$ for $u \geq 0$ and an appropriate growth bound on $f$, a convex relaxation of the action functional yields the existence of a positive weak solution. Furthermore, we prove that in this setting, and under a slightly stronger sign condition $$f(x,u) > 0\text{ for }u > 0,$$ all global minimizers of the action functional do not vanish in $(-1,1)$ but fail to be of class $C^1$.

title: A tractable transition function for the Wright-Fisher diffusion with selection via gamma duality
abstract: The transition function of the Wright-Fisher diffusion with selection is a fundamental object for non-neutral evolutionary modelling and likelihood-based inference, but, unlike in the neutral case, existing representations are impractical or inefficient. Spectral approaches rely on truncation levels that grow with selection strength and the number of alleles, thus leading to rapidly increasing computational costs, while existing duality-based expansions lead to multi-type dual processes whose transition probabilities involve intractable normalising constants. In this paper we obtain a new transition-function representation for the multi-allelic Wright-Fisher diffusion with parent-independent mutation and genic selection that makes transition-law evaluation and simulation practically feasible in regimes where existing methods are costly or unavailable. The key tool is a new gamma duality, obtained by augmenting classical polynomial duality by an exponential tilting and yields a multivariate birth-death dual with fully explicit infinitesimal rates and an entrance-boundary construction. This is used to express the Wright-Fisher transition law as an explicit mixture of standard Dirichlet components, with mixing weights obtained from the dual started from its entrance boundary. We characterise the dual stationary distribution and its small-time behaviour, and develop practical and efficient sampling procedures for both transition and stationary laws, including a fast approximate stationary sampler with explicit error control. Numerical experiments illustrate substantial runtime gains over specialised methods in regimes where they apply, while our approach remains applicable for arbitrary numbers of alleles and selection coefficients.

title: Weak and strong discretization errors for signatures of Gaussian processes
abstract: Let $X$ be a continuous Gaussian process in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, with independent components of roughness $H\in(\tfrac14,1)$, possibly with a linear drift, and let $X^n$ be its piecewise-linear interpolant on a mesh of width $δ$. We study how well the truncated signature of $X^n$ approximates that of the natural lift of $X$, in mean (the weak error) and in $L^2$ (the strong error). Over a class of drivers defined by quantitative regularity conditions, the weak error at every fixed truncation level is $O(δ^{γ(H)})$ with $γ(H)=\min(2H,4H-1)$, uniformly over the class, and for truncation levels $M\ge4$ fractional Brownian motion attains this rate. For centred drivers the weak error vanishes at levels $1$ to $3$, Gaussian or not. It first appears at level~$4$, where we compute its leading constant for independent fractional Brownian motion in $d=2$: on $(\tfrac12,1)$ it is $1/(2\sqrt3)$, independent of $H$, and on $(\tfrac14,\tfrac12)$ it is given by a $ζ$-series. For fractional Brownian motion with drift, a level-$3$ error of the same order appears for $H\ge\tfrac12$. Below $\tfrac12$ the drift reaches the rate only at levels $\ge5$ (proved for $d\ge3$). The strong error is of exact order $δ^{2H-1/2}$ for fractional Brownian motion with $H\in(\tfrac12,1)$, so in mean square the weak error lies a full power of $δ$ below it. For $H\le\tfrac12$ the strong error is $O(δ^{\vartheta})$ for every $\vartheta<2H-\tfrac12$, uniformly over the class, and the exponent $2H-\tfrac12$ cannot be improved. Finally, we construct pairs of laws in the class whose mesh data have the same law but whose expected signatures differ by order $δ^{γ(H)}$. Hence no quantity computed from the mesh data has mean within $o(δ^{γ(H)})$ of the expected signature uniformly over the class.

title: Joint Approximation and the Mixed-Prime Character Group
abstract: For the integer metric defined by the square denominators of two distinct primes, we prove simultaneous approximation to zero in one prime metric and to any prescribed integer in the other. A normalized convolution argument gives a uniform central spectral bound. Random relative translations of smooth weights produce an exact positive cas cade; Fourier positivity places every normalized finer convolution below its value at zero. A far-field recursion, the growth of merged square powers, and a two-term logarithmic-form estimate give summable fac tor bounds. Consequently, for every fixed pair of distinct primes p,q, the mixed continuous character group is Z[1/(pq)]/Z: no irrational pa rameter is continuous. The mixed completion is the product of the one-prime completions. For each fixed pair this also gives a compati ble rational join and a strictly finer compatible join of the associated real TVG topologies, with the same prescribed real character group. Exact witness search terminates at every strict precision and integer target. We retain the structural, density, divisibility, sequence and finite-certificate results leading to this proof. The existence argument does not give practical witness-size or runtime bounds, and it does not assume independence or equidistribution of the two digit systems. Se lected abstract components have been checked using Lean and Mathlib; the complete analytic argument has not been formalized. The corre sponding problem for three or more primes remains separate.

title: A Poincare-Einstein Liouville Theorem and the Yamabe Invariant of Lens Spaces
abstract:
Schoen conjectured that the Yamabe invariant of every lens space is achieved by the round metric. A proof of this conjecture is presented for all lens spaces, together with rigidity: equality is only achieved for the round class. The key step is to show that every $\mathbb Z_p$-invariant Yamabe-positive conformal class on $S^3$ admits a $\mathbb Z_p$-equivariant Poincaré-Einstein filling. The distance function from a fixed point of the filling then gives an invariant test function with Yamabe quotient at most $σ(S^3)$, which descends to the lens space.
  The proof of the main theorem was generated by AI (ChatGPT Astra, September 2026); this is mainly a learning note of the AI generated proof.

title: Task-Contribution Dynamics of Adam in Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Slow-Manifold Analysis and Gradient Modulation
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often suffer from imbalanced optimization of competing loss components, particularly when approximating solutions with high-frequency or multiscale features. Although existing balancing strategies have proven effective in alleviating this difficulty, the mechanisms governing the evolution of individual task contributions to Adam's parameter updates remain insufficiently understood. We introduce task-wise indicators to characterize this evolution and identify three distinct training regimes: smooth variation, intermittent spikes, and persistent oscillations. Focusing on the early smooth regime, we combine discrete-time analysis with a continuous-time singular perturbation framework under the full-batch setting and the parameter regime $(1-β_2)/(1-β_1)\ll1$. A first-order approximation of the locally attracting slow manifold reveals two factors governing the step-to-step redistribution of task contributions: curvature-related alignment disparities and differences in the coordinatewise distributions of preconditioned task gradients. Both factors involve Adam's shared second-moment estimate. Inspired by AdaTask, we propose Gradient-Modulated Adam (GMAdam), which modulates incoming task gradients using task-specific second-moment estimates. Numerical experiments on high-frequency Poisson and wave equations, the Allen-Cahn equation, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity flow ($Re=100,400$) demonstrate consistent improvements in predictive accuracy over AdaTask at comparable computational cost.

title: Empirical approximation of $L_p$ norms for $p\in (2, \infty)$
abstract: For $p>2$ and an $N$-dimensional subspace $X\subset L_\infty(μ)$ satisfying \[ \|f\|_\infty\le (KN)^{1/p}\|f\|_{L_p(μ)} \quad\forall f\in X, \] we show that $m\ge C(p)KN \bigl(\varepsilon^{-p} +\varepsilon^{-2}\log_2(2N)\bigr)$ independent samples $ξ^1,\ldots,ξ^m$ with distribution $μ$ satisfy \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(ξ^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \quad\forall f\in X \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c(p)\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This gives the optimal sample-size order $N\log_2 N$ for independent random sampling with fixed $K$, $p$, and $\varepsilon$. This result follows from a more general empirical moment estimate over unit balls of $p$-convex norms.

title: Differentiation of tepui groupoids and the holonomy groupoid of singular foliations
abstract: Tepui groupoids are a generalization of Lie groupoids which allow the arrow space to be singular, as is the case for holonomy groupoids of singular foliations. We construct a Lie differentiation functor for a large class of tepui groupoids. When restricted to effective and source-connected tepui groupoids, this differentiation recovers the correspondence between holonomy groupoids and their underlying singular foliations.

title: Left-Invariant Kernels of the Hodge-de Rham Operator on Three-Dimensional Lorentzian Lie Groups
abstract: We determine the kernel of the Hodge--de Rham operator on left-invariant differential forms for the seven customary families of three-dimensional Lorentzian metric Lie algebras. Every parameter stratum is treated, including zero structure constants, singular bracket matrices, and null modular directions. If $θ(X)=\mathrm{tr}\,\mathrm{ad}_X$ is the modular character, the full kernel is the direct sum of constants, the space $K=\mathrm{Ann}([\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{g}])\capθ^\perp$, its Hodge dual, and the volume forms. We give explicit real bases in all seven families and compute the exterior differential and geometric codifferential on every basis form. The non-unimodular calculation remains valid without the customary extra normalization conditions, and hence also covers metric representatives omitted by those conditions. The resulting dimensions are $2,4,6$, or $8$; the two middle-degree dimensions agree. Explicit examples distinguish the kernel of the first-order operator from the kernel of its square. All assertions concern smooth left-invariant forms, with no square-integrability condition.

title: Proof of the Cordero-Torregrosa Conjecture and an Improved Order Bound for Paired Jacobian Evaluations
abstract:
In solving systems of nonlinear equations, one of the main objectives is to construct iterative methods that attain high orders of convergence using as few evaluations as possible. However, the information a method obtains during each iteration imposes limitations on the order it can guarantee. The Cordero--Torregrosa conjecture proposes a bound on this order in terms of the number of evaluations of the function and its Jacobian.
  In this work, we prove this bound for the universal local order of one iteration, without requiring the number of Jacobian evaluations to be less than or equal to the number of function evaluations. In particular, our result also covers the case in which more evaluations of the Jacobian than of the function are performed. The proof encompasses deterministic, causal, memoryless methods whose rules may be arbitrary, without imposing rationality, continuity, or computability conditions.
  Moreover, we prove that when each Jacobian evaluation is performed at a point where the value of the function is already known, a more restrictive bound on the order of convergence can be obtained. Finally, we propose a new conjecture that establishes a refined bound through a product of factors determined by the distribution of evaluations, under additional dimensional conditions. These results provide a better understanding of the limitations imposed by the available information and raise new possibilities for studying high-order iterative methods.

title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
abstract: We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.

title: Talanov dynamics and chirp-controlled rogue-wave formation for the vector nonlinear Schrödinger equation
abstract: We study the focusing vector nonlinear Schrödinger equation, or Manakov system, for a pair of coupled initial conditions with compactly supported, concave parabolic density profiles and phases depending quadratically on the spatial coordinate. We focus on the natural class of self-similar solutions generated by such profiles, whose dispersionless evolution we refer to as Talanov dynamics. We extend the criterion for blow-up in finite time, first established for a single field, to the Manakov case. For arbitrary initial chirps in the two fields, we provide closed-form expressions for their evolution, and an explicit expression for the time of the gradient catastrophe, if it occurs, and we classify the effect of the coupling on the catastrophe. Depending on the initial chirps, the two fields may catastrophise, or relax, as each would if decoupled. However, coupling can also force the catastrophe in fields that would otherwise relax if decoupled. For identical initial supports, and in the presence of dispersion, we numerically show that the same dispersionless criterion determines, in the semiclassical regime, whether the fully dispersive solution relaxes or develops a rogue wave in each field, whose onset time is accurately predicted by the corresponding dispersionless catastrophe time, in direct analogy with the scalar case. As chirp and amplitude are relatively easy to control experimentally, we expect these results to be relevant to experiments in nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates, extending to coupled systems observations made for the scalar equation.

title: Cantor's onion: a uniformly quasiregular map whose Julia set is a Cantor set of spheres
abstract: For integers $d,m\ge2$ with $1/d+1/m<1$, we construct a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{S}^3$ of degree $d^2+m^2$ whose Julia set is a Cantor set of concentric round spheres. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a uniformly quasiregular map in dimension three with infinitely many Fatou components. The map is a three-dimensional analogue of McMullen's maps $z^d+λ/z^m$, built from two Zorich-type power maps glued across a single shell by a slit construction. Its Julia set has Hausdorff dimension $2+s$, where $d^{-s}+m^{-s}=1$, and the restriction of the map to its Julia set is a skew product over the shift on two symbols and has topological entropy $\log(d^2+m^2)$. We also prove that uniformly quasiregular maps that expand uniformly near their Julia set, possibly with branching there, have no wandering domains and only finitely many periodic Fatou components, all of them attracting basins. The map constructed here belongs to this class.

title: An Asymptotic Framework for Closed-Form Estimators from Surrogate Estimating Equations
abstract: Many statistical estimators, including maximum likelihood and method of moments estimators, are defined as roots of estimating equations. In complex models, these equations often cannot be solved explicitly; although numerical methods can provide approximate solutions, closed-form approximations can reduce computation and facilitate theoretical analysis by making an estimator's dependence on the data more transparent. In this paper, we develop a general approach to constructing such approximations and a framework for quantifying their accuracy. Our theory accommodates sequences of parameters that approach the boundary of the parameter space or diverge to infinity, and provides conditions under which a closed-form approximate estimator has the same first-order asymptotic distribution as its exact counterpart. We focus on approximations to maximum likelihood estimators, although the theory applies to general estimating equations. We apply the framework to iid models from the gamma, zeta, von Mises, and generalized Pareto families, as well as to gamma regression. Together, these examples cover scalar and vector parameters, iid and non-iid settings, and normal and nonnormal asymptotic regimes. Each example is accompanied by a simulation study, and the gamma regression example also includes a real-world data application.

title: EDP-PI-DOSnet: An Energy Dissipation Preserving Neural Solver for Two-Phase Flow Problems
abstract: Preserving the energy dissipation properties of gradient flow equations is important for the stability and reliability of numerical approximations, particularly in long-time simulations. In this paper, we propose a class of energy-dissipation-preserving physics-informed deep operator splitting networks (EDP-PI-DOSnets) for solving gradient flow equations. The proposed framework incorporates classical structure-preserving numerical schemes into neural network architectures, allowing the corresponding discrete energy dissipation laws to be preserved. In particular, suitable constraints are imposed on the convolution kernels to ensure that the learned discrete operators are symmetric and negative semidefinite. Furthermore, several network formulations are developed based on the Crank--Nicolson (CN), scalar auxiliary variable Crank--Nicolson (SAV/CN), and relaxed discrete variational derivative (R-DVD-1) schemes. Meanwhile, a physics-informed loss function based on the residuals of the governing equations is employed. Numerical experiments show that the predicted solutions are in good agreement with the reference solutions while satisfying the corresponding discrete energy dissipation laws. The results also suggest stable behavior during long-time recursive prediction and the potential applicability of the proposed framework to two-phase flow problems.

title: Kolmogorov Obstacle Problems: Euclidean Free Boundary Regularity under a Cone Condition
abstract: We study obstacle problems for Kolmogorov-type operators that diffuse in one variable and transport in another. Such problems describe American options on running averages. Under a cone estimate, a strong monotonicity condition on the solution in the diffusive direction, we show that the free boundary is a graph in the diffusive direction with Hölder continuous first derivatives in the Euclidean sense, and that every free boundary point is regular. The key observation is that a Euclidean Lipschitz free boundary is flat at the intrinsic scale. For the American fixed-strike Asian option we verify the cone estimate, so that its exercise boundary has the same regularity.

title: Commuting Toeplitz and Little Hankel Operators on the Bidisk
abstract: Necessary and sufficient conditions are obtained for two Toeplitz operators and for a Toeplitz operator and a little Hankel operator to commute on the pluriharmonic Hardy space of the bidisk.

title: The Woo-Yong conjecture
abstract: We prove the Woo-Yong conjecture: the non-Gorenstein locus of a type A Schubert variety is the union of its generically non-Gorenstein maximal singular components. More strongly, at every scheme point, local Weil divisor classes are detected at the generic points of the maximal singular components containing that point. For arbitrary finite crystallographic type, the analogous localization map is injective on the torsion subgroup of the source local class group. This determines Cartier indices of locally $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisors and gives the Woo-Yong criterion on the $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein locus. A type D family shows the necessity of this hypothesis: the ambient variety is generically Gorenstein along its singular locus but not $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein along a deeper nonempty locus. The type A proof and the counterexamples are geometric; the general torsion proof also uses bounded finite inputs with explicit certificates and reproducible reconstruction programs.

title: Boundary singularities for the Lane-Emden equation
abstract: For every $n\ge3$ and $(n+1)/(n-1)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct positive solutions of $Δu+u^p=0$ in the half-space with zero Dirichlet data away from the origin, the homogeneous singular profile there, and Poisson-kernel decay at infinity, resolving a question of del Pino--Musso--Pacard. Under a weighted non-degeneracy condition, these half-space solutions serve as building blocks for positive very weak solutions in smooth bounded domains, singular along prescribed compact smooth boundary submanifolds of normal dimension $n$. We verify non-degeneracy in the initial stable interval and at and just beyond its threshold when this lies below $(n+2)/(n-2)$. For isolated boundary singularities, the construction applies throughout the strict subcritical interval outside a locally finite exceptional set.

title: Entropy and frame measures for self-similar measures
abstract:
For $0<ρ<1$ and a set of $N\ge2$ distinct real digits $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\mathbb{R}$, let \[
  μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}=\frac1N\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}\circ S_i^{-1},
  \qquad S_i(x)=ρ(x+d_i). \] Write $X=\sum_{j\ge1}ρ^j d_{ω_j}$, where the symbols $ω_j$ are independent and uniform on $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$. We prove that $μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy $H(ω_1\mid X)>0$. In particular, this holds for all $ρ>1/N$, without any absolute-continuity assumption or arithmetic restriction on the digits or the contraction. At $ρ=1/N$, for commensurable digits, a frame measure exists if and only if $μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor. For $\mathscr D=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ and $ρ<1/N$, we also prove nonexistence whenever $ρ^{-m}=a/b$ for some $m\in\N$, with $a/b$ in lowest terms, $b\mid N$ and $N/b\nmid a$, extending the integer-power obstruction. The extension compares mask quotients using finite families of target pole classes in place of one target class.

title: Construction of DAE solver Rodas4PW and numerical test examples with Rosenbrock and W-methods in OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl
abstract: This paper compares various Rosenbrock and Rosenbrock W-methods. To achieve this, some methods implemented in the Julia package OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl are selected and benchmarked using test examples. The test examples include stiff ODE problems as well as differential-algebraic equations. In addition to the already known methods, the new W-method Rodas4PW is introduced and included in the tests.

title: A Dirichlet form approach to the potential theory of $m$-subharmonic functions
abstract:
On a bounded open subset of $\mathbb{C}^n$, we study the Dirichlet form induced by an admissible pair $(θ,μ)$, where $μ$ is a positive Radon measure and $$θ=dd^c u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^c u_{m-1}\wedge(dd^c \lvert z\rvert^2)^{n-m}$$ for locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions $u_1,\dots,u_{m-1}$. We prove that locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions belong locally to the domains of these Dirichlet forms and are quasi-continuous with respect to the induced capacities. We establish a monotonicity property for Dirichlet forms, which motivates the introduction of $μ$-quasi-monotone convergence of $m$-subharmonic functions. The natural embeddings into these domains are continuous with respect to this convergence. These results yield new proofs of the commutativity and continuity of complex Hessian operators.
  Using this framework, we characterize quasi-continuity with respect to the induced capacity for an arbitrary $m$-subharmonic function in terms of its pole set having zero measure $μ$, or equivalently, zero induced capacity. On bounded strictly $m$-pseudoconvex domains, we prove that the Bedford--Taylor capacity for $m$-subharmonic functions and the capacities induced by the corresponding Dirichlet forms have the same null sets. We further characterize $m$-polar sets in terms of Dirichlet forms and stochastic processes, extending the corresponding characterization of pluripolar sets due to Fukushima and Okada to the $m$-subharmonic setting.

title: Erratum to: Monotonicity of Ursell functions in the Ising model
abstract: In this note, we correct an error in the proof Theorem 1 of Comm. Math. Phys. 401 (2023), 2459-2482.

title: Spectral Characterizations, Harmonic Analysis, and Phase Transitions in 2-Nice and $k$-Nice Recurrence
abstract: We investigate the structural mechanisms governing $2$-nice and $k$-nice recurrence in measure-preserving dynamical systems. For weakly mixing systems, we establish a complete spectral characterization of two-sided $2$-nice recurrence via quadratic spectral functionals and Herglotz--Bochner duality, extending the theory to arbitrary integer polynomial configurations $\{0, p_1(n), p_2(n)\}$ with zero constant term and to actions of countable abelian groups. Using stationary Gaussian processes and Hermite mode decoupling, we construct explicit weakly mixing counterexamples separating one-sided and two-sided $2$-nice recurrence. Furthermore, we uncover a fundamental structural phase transition at $k=3$: while $k=2$ recurrence is rigidly controlled by a quadratic spectral functional whose two-sided symmetrization eliminates all higher-degree cumulants, at $k=3$ fourth-order centered correlations survive symmetrization and can drive a strict recurrence deficit even when the quadratic spectral functional remains strictly positive. Using lacunary and multi-frequency Riesz products alongside uniform Wiener lemmas, we analyze the upper Banach density obstructions of negative spectral sets, establish partial partition regularity on the spectral cone, resolve an inverse Furstenberg correspondence problem of Rodríguez Martín for countable groups via Bernoulli product extensions, and characterize spectral $2$-nice ultrafilters in the Stone--Čech compactification $β\N$.

title: Elastic Wave Imaging via Kirchhoff Migration: Resolution Analysis and Inclusion Identification
abstract: We consider the inverse problem of determining the location, orientation, shape, and material parameters of a small elastic inclusion embedded in a homogeneous medium from full-aperture measurements of the scattered field. Using a small-volume expansion, we derive explicit leading-order expressions for four Kirchhoff migration imaging functionals, denoted by PP, PS, SP, and SS, corresponding to the four combinations of pressure (P) and shear (S) waves used for receiver- and source-side backpropagation. The resulting point-spread functions quantitatively characterize the resolution of each mode and show that the SS mode achieves the highest spatial resolution. For an elliptic inclusion, we show that the PP mode uniquely determines the elastic moment tensor (EMT) within the leading-order asymptotic model, thereby enabling the reconstruction of the material and geometric parameters of the inclusion. For a general small scatterer, the reconstruction may instead be interpreted as an effective elliptic representation determined by its leading-order EMT. For a disk, the parameter-identification problem is underdetermined; nevertheless, explicit upper and lower bounds on its volume are derived. We further analyze the model error arising from neglected cross-mode contributions when the distance from the center of the measurement configuration is not sufficiently large relative to the elastic wavelengths. Numerical experiments support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed imaging and reconstruction methods.

title: Formalization of Filter-Method Construction for Real Numbers in Coq
abstract: This paper presents a formalization for a theory of constructing real numbers using concepts related to filters. The formalization is implemented using the Coq proof assistant and is grounded in axiomatic set theory. The theory encompasses various notions such as filters, ultrafilters, principal ultrafilters, and arithmetical ultrafilters. A special filter, namely the non-principal arithmetical ultrafilter, whose existence requires the Continuum Hypothesis to be proven, is employed to establish several non-standard number sets: *N, *Z and *Q. The set of real numbers, R, is subsequently derived by equivalently classifying a specific subset of *Q. The entire theory is thoroughly formalized, with each detail verified to ensure rigor and precision. This work contributes a new selection of foundational materials for the formalization of mathematical theories.

title: Byzantine-Robust Distributed Sparse Softmax Regression
abstract: We study Byzantine-robust distributed sparse softmax regression in high-dimensional settings. We propose a communication-efficient distributed algorithm that employs robust aggregation methods---coordinate-wise trimmed mean and coordinate-wise median---to defend against Byzantine attacks. Under sub-Gaussian design assumptions with sparsity constraints, we establish that the distributed estimator achieves the convergence rate of $O_{P}(K^{\frac{5}{2}}\sqrt{s\log(Kd)/N})$ when the Byzantine fraction $α\asymp 1/\sqrt{m}$, matching the centralized oracle rate. Numerical experiments on synthetic data demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method.

title: Cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension
abstract: We define cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension over fields of characteristic zero, extending the definition for curves by Grothendieck. Our notion of cuspidal sections is defined relative to a normal crossings compactification. We prove that the closure of the resulting set is independent of the choice of a compactification. For varieties iteratively constructed from fibrations, we compare our definition to an inductive notion of cuspidal sections, and discuss connections to the section conjecture of Grothendieck.

title: Ore-degree conditions for matchings in uniform hypergraphs
abstract: Let $σ_r(\mathcal{H})$ be the minimum sum of vertex degrees over all nonedges of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ on $n$ vertices. Balogh, Palmer and Raeisi conjectured that $n>2rs$ and $σ_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ imply the existence of a matching of size $s$ in $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that, for every fixed $r\ge3$ and all sufficiently large $s$, $σ_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ forces an $s$-matching whenever $n\ge rs+\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$. A complete $r$-graph on $rs-1$ vertices together with $\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$ isolated vertices shows that the vertex bound is sharp for all sufficiently large $s$. By adding new vertices to $\mathcal{H}$, retaining all its edges, and adding every $r$-set containing at least one new vertex as an edge, we also deduce that $n\ge rs+C$ suffices under the same degree condition for every $s\ge1$, where $C$ is a finite constant depending only on $r$. For $r=3$, we provide the explicit sufficient order $n\ge\lceil(7s+11)/2\rceil$ for $s\ge6$, together with bounds for $2\le s\le5$, establishing the conjecture in this uniformity. For $s=2$, we improve the known sufficient order $2r+2$ to $2r+1$ for every $r\ge3$ and show that this order is best possible.

title: Cable Knot Counterexamples to the All-Knot Volume Conjecture
abstract: Let $E$ be the figure-eight knot and let $V$ be the hyperbolic volume of its exterior. We study the reduced colored Jones polynomial at $q=e^{2πi/N}$ for the $(p,w)$-cable of the connected sum of $d\ge 2$ copies of $E$, where $w\ge 2$ and $p,w$ are coprime. The normalized logarithmic growth rate converges to the JSJ volume $dV$ along colors coprime to $2w$, and its upper limit along colors sharing a divisor with $w$ is at most $V$. Thus the $(1,2)$-cable of $E\#E$ violates the full-sequence volume limit for knots. The $(1,3)$-cable of the same companion shows that convergence can fail even along all odd colors. The separation comes from the multiples of $N$ in the exact cabling sum and a uniform first-derivative estimate for the other companion colors.

title: A semi-implicit exactly well-balanced relaxation scheme for the 2d shallow water system
abstract: We propose a semi-implicit, exactly well-balanced finite volume scheme for the two-dimensional shallow water equations over a non-flat bottom, aimed at the low-Froude-number regime. The method combines a Suliciu-type relaxation of the pressure with a flux splitting that separates the fast acoustic waves from the slow transport ones: the pressure subsystem is integrated implicitly and the transport subsystem explicitly, so that the time step is no longer restricted by the acoustic stability condition. Written in terms of its Riemann invariants, the pressure subsystem decouples into independent one-dimensional problems along the grid lines, each of them governed by a banded linear system whose bandwidth does not depend on the mesh. The implicit step therefore requires no non-linear solver and costs O(NxNy) operations, regardless of the acoustic Courant number. A two-dimensional exactly well-balanced reconstruction, whose limiter weights are frozen within each time step, preserves this linear structure for the second-order scheme. We prove that both the first- and the second-order schemes preserve water-at-rest equilibria exactly, and we assess them on several two-dimensional benchmarks, where they resolve fine-scale velocity structures on coarse meshes and run up to 8.5 times faster than standard explicit Riemann solvers.

title: Two-step nilpotent varieties as categories of modules over a square ring
abstract: We characterise the two-step nilpotent varieties of algebras: the semi-abelian varieties in which all ternary cosmash products vanish. Just as abelian varieties are the categories of modules over a ring, two-step nilpotent varieties are exactly the categories of modules over a square ring in the sense of Baues, Hartl and Pirashvili. We construct the square ring explicitly from the full subcategory on the free algebras on one and two generators, and give complete proofs. As consequences we obtain a description of any two-step nilpotent variety by generators and relations, an intrinsic characterisation in terms of quadratic term operations, and an account of its abelian core and of the lower central series of its objects in terms of the square ring. Along the way, we associate with any commutative ring $R$ a square ring whose modules, the two-step nilpotent $R$-groups, extend Hall's nilpotent $R$-groups of class two from $2$-binomial rings to arbitrary rings of coefficients.

title: Weighted \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal{O}$}-operators on pre-Leibniz algebras and post-pre-Leibniz structures
abstract: In this paper, we introduce weighted $\mathcal{O}$-operators (also called weighted relative Rota-Baxter operators) on pre-Leibniz algebras. We construct a differential graded Lie algebra whose Maurer-Cartan elements are exactly these operators. This allows us to define their cohomology as that of the induced pre-Leibniz algebra with coefficients in a suitable representation. As an application, we study formal and finite order deformations of these operators. We show that this theory splits the corresponding theory for weighted $\mathcal{O}$-operators on Leibniz algebras. Finally, we introduce post-pre-Leibniz algebras as the algebraic structures underlying weighted $\mathcal{O}$-operators on pre-Leibniz algebras.

title: Every countable group has the nonsingular weak Rokhlin property
abstract: We prove that for every countable group $Γ$, in the space of nonsingular actions by $Γ$, there is an action whose orbit under conjugation is dense. This is the nonsingular analogue of the result of Glasner, Thouvenot, and Weiss that every countable group $Γ$ is weak Rokhlin, i.e., there is a dense orbit in the space of probability measure preserving $Γ$-actions.

title: Sharp isoperimetry in groups of polynomial growth
abstract: We study weighted edge boundary and outer vertex boundary on Cayley graphs of polynomial growth of degree $Q>1$. For every finite symmetric generating set, we prove that each exact isoperimetric profile satisfies $I(n)=c n^{(Q-1)/Q}+O(n^{(Q-1)/Q-β})$, where $β=1/(8Q^2)$. We identify the leading constant with the isoperimetric constant of a horizontal perimeter on the limiting Carnot group, after accounting for the counting density. Its integrand is a norm with polyhedral unit ball, determined by a convex minimization with one real variable for each coset of a torsion-free nilpotent subgroup. For every asymptotically minimizing sequence, we translate its vertex sets so that the characteristic functions of the associated rescaled regions are precompact in $L^1$. The limiting regions minimize continuum perimeter at fixed volume. The exact-cardinality estimate requires no regularity assumption on these regions. For virtually abelian groups, we prove a quantitative stability estimate using a discrete approximation to the Euclidean Wulff body. The relative symmetric difference from a translate is bounded by the square root of the sum of the relative boundary deficit and a cardinality error. We also characterize when bounded additive changes of Cayley metric preserve the leading vertex constant. Failure occurs already in rank two; we construct pairs with the same measured asymptotic cone whose leading constants have an unbounded ratio as the rank grows.

title: Asymptotic behavior of solutions to the critical $p$-Laplace equation near isolated singularities
abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of weak solutions to the following critical $p$-Laplace equation \[ -Δ_p u=u^{p^*-1}, \quad u\ge0 \quad\hbox{in }B_1\setminus\{0\}, \] where $Δ_pu=\diver(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u)$ is the classical $p$-Laplacian with $1<p<n$, $p^*=\frac{np}{n-p}$ is the Sobolev critical exponent and $B_1\setminus\{0\}\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is the punctured unit ball. We develop a nonlinear potential-theoretic method to establish sharp upper bounds for solutions, without using the method of moving planes or moving spheres. Furthermore, we use Steiner symmetrization to study the radial symmetry of global singular solutions, and thereby classify all Fowler singular solutions. Finally, we prove that every local singular solution is asymptotic to a global Fowler singular solution.

title: Trace and Regularized Index of Callias Operators on Hyperbolic Space
abstract: Let $d \geq 3$ be odd. On hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$, we consider Callias-type operators, i.e. Dirac-Schrödinger operators of the form $D = ic \nabla + A$, where $c \nabla$ is the Dirac operator and $A$ a function with values in the self-adjoint operators, and provide an explicit formula for the iterated trace $\text{tr}_{L^2(\mathbb{H}^d,H)} \text{tr}_{S}( e^{-tD^*D} - e^{-tDD^*})$, $t>0$, that appears in the formulation of the Witten index. Thereby, the operator $D$ is not assumed to be Fredholm.

title: Zak Phase, Pole--Zero Invariants and the Maslov Index of Bloch Cauchy Lines in One-Dimensional Periodic Media
abstract: The topological properties of the Bloch bands of a one-dimensional periodic medium are described either by the Berry--Zak phase or by the poles and zeros of the surface impedance. We show that both can be read from one geometric object: the line spanned by the field and its flux (the Cauchy data) at an inversion centre. For each band, this line turns as the quasi-momentum runs over the Brillouin zone. Its number of turns, the Maslov index, is fixed by the parities (even or odd) of the Bloch functions at the two band edges, and its parity is the Zak phase. In a gap, the Cauchy line of the solution decaying on one side rotates monotonically with the energy, and an interface state between two crystals is a crossing of two such lines. This gives the known criterion of at most one state per gap in terms of the same lines. Examples with a stratified medium show that the choice of inversion centre changes the interface spectrum. The last section discusses what is missing to extend the construction to higher dimension.

title: The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers among polynomial values
abstract: Let $φ$ be a fixed polynomial with integer coefficients, positive leading coefficient and degree $k\geq2$. We prove that the values $2φ(n)$, $1\leq n\leq N$, can be written as the sum of two primes, apart from at most $N^{α_k+o(1)}$ exceptional indices, where $α_k<1$. For quadratic polynomials the exponent is $1/2$, for cubic polynomials $5/8$, for quartic polynomials $3/4$, and for $k>4$ it is $1-1/(k+1)$. The proof combines a fourth-moment estimate over primes with mean-value estimates over arbitrary subsets of polynomial sequences.

title: Universal Decoding for Gaussian MIMO-ISI: Spherical Ensembles and Symmetric Neighborhoods
abstract: We construct a universal decoder for cyclic Gaussian multiple-input multiple-output channels with intersymbol interference and unknown channel taps and spatial noise covariance. Codewords are drawn independently and uniformly from a sphere of fixed total energy. Under stated bounds on frequency variation, the decoder attains the ensemble-average error exponent of informed maximum-likelihood decoding for fixed channels and channels with growing memory. We approximate the frequency response by a constant matrix within each frequency block. For this auxiliary channel, every matched log-likelihood is affine in a common sufficient statistic. At fixed received output, we compute the statistic density of an independent competitor. The decoder selects the candidate with the smallest statistic density, equivalently minimizing a weighted sum of residual log-determinants. The density and its support volume give an upper bound on the universal competitor probability. Affinity ensures that at least half of a suitable symmetric neighborhood of the transmitted statistic has matched likelihood no smaller than that of the transmitted word. Integrating a density lower bound over this half gives the matched competitor bound. These bounds establish equality of error exponents, which a Gaussian channel comparison transfers to the original channel. The same decoder attains the matched exponent for independent frequency blocks with prescribed energies satisfying the stated conditions. For energies proportional to block length, an additional gain condition ensures that this exponent is at least that of the total-energy spherical ensemble.

title: Anchored Iterative Decoding of Reed-Solomon Product Codes for High-Rate Magnetic Tape Storage
abstract: We present a decoding algorithm for a Reed--Solomon product code targeted at the demanding reliability requirements of modern magnetic tape storage. For a code $RS(256, 224)\times RS(175, 173)$ in a BSC we achieve post-decoding bit error rate (BER) of $10^{-20}$ at $\approx 5.3\times 10^{-3}$ raw BER while maintaining the common requirement to detect and correct 4 out of 32 dead tracks. We resolve two common problems of miscorrections and stall patterns that arise under such a high raw BER via simplified versions of anchor decoding and binary image analysis. The highest efficiency is achieved by performing an unlimited iterative decoder, which performs decoding iterations until no changes are made. We give an empirical analysis of the average number of iterations: below the raw BER of $5\times 10^{-3}$, four half-iterations are performed on average while improving substantially over a decoder that always performs 4 half-iterations. We provide a CPU implementation achieving 100-200 megabytes/s single-core throughput on a regular laptop and a design of a potential hybrid FPGA-CPU implementation of our decoder.

title: Tetragonal conic bundles
abstract: This paper addresses the birational geometry of three-dimensional algebraic varieties admitting a conic bundle structure. The central focus is on tetragonal transformations -- a special class of birational maps between standard conic bundles that are not fiberwise and play a key role in the birational geometry of such varieties.

title: Unique ergodicity of systems of finite order and the density finite sums theorem in arbitrary abelian groups
abstract: Let $Γ$ be a countable abelian group and $k\geq 1$. We establish that every minimal topological $Γ$-system of order $k$ is uniquely ergodic. This result, which was previously only known for finitely generated groups for arbitrary $k$, answers a question of Glasner, Gutman, and Ye and yields the answer to multiple questions by Candela, González-Sánchez, and Szegedy. As applications of our dynamical results, we obtain the following combinatorial theorems. Let $A\subseteq Γ$ be a set of positive upper Banach density. Then there are infinite sets $B_1,\ldots, B_k\subseteq Γ$ such that $B_1+\dots+B_k\subseteq A$. If $Γ$ satisfies a necessary divisibility assumption, then there are also $t\in Γ$ and an infinite set $B\subseteq Γ$ such that $A-t$ contains the set of all sums of $m$ pairwise distinct elements of $B$ for all $m\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$. For arbitrary $k$, these density finite sums theorems were only known in the integers previously.

title: One complex metric and geometric adelic nefness
abstract: We prove that an arithmetic adelic line bundle on a smooth quasi-projective variety over a number field has nef geometric part if its prescribed continuous metric at one complex embedding has semipositive first Chern current. The proof constructs semiample approximations to every positive rational ample perturbation by boundary extension, multiplier ideals, and Nadel vanishing, followed by specialization and Galois descent. This gives geometric nefness of Gao--Zhang's canonical Gross--Schoen adelic line bundle.

title: A sharp weighted $L^2$ Bernstein inequality for partial derivatives on the unit ball
abstract: We determine the sharp constant in the weighted $L^2$ Bernstein inequality for coordinate derivatives on the unit ball with a Jacobi weight and the strengthened derivative factors introduced by Beberok and Xu. The constant is expressed in terms of the largest zeros of Jacobi polynomials, and all extremal polynomials are characterized explicitly. The proof uses an orthogonal polynomial decomposition that gives diagonal formulas for both the squared norm and the weighted derivative integral. We also obtain two-sided bounds for the sharp constant and determine its leading asymptotic behavior as the polynomial degree tends to infinity.

title: Natural potentials for TT tensors, divergence-free symmetric tensors and linearised relativistic initial data
abstract: Let $N$ be a natural tensor which vanishes at a metric $g\_0$. By diffeomorphism invariance, $DN(g\_0)^*$ takes values in divergence-free symmetric $2$-tensors, and in TT tensors if moreover $DN(g\_0)$ kills conformal directions. Such operators are local potentials, which we call machines: they produce smooth compactly supported tensors with the required property and, on closed manifolds, all of them up to a finite-dimensional space when their symbol is injective. On Einstein manifolds of every dimension, the linearised Bach tensor gives the operator $P$ of an earlier paper, which factorises on TT tensors into the massless and partially massless spin-$2$ operators; we also construct machines on Bach-flat, conformally flat and Ricci-parallel metrics. Replacing the diffeomorphisms of $M$ by those of the vacuum development, we obtain potentials, with a Fredholm property, for the linearised Einstein constraint equations on arbitrary spacelike hypersurfaces of Minkowski, de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes.

title: The enigma of locally Toeplitz matrices. I. Discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential
abstract: Freezing the coefficients of a banded locally Toeplitz matrix gives a family of Toeplitz eigenvalue measures. Their average can fill a region of the complex plane even when the eigenvalues of the original matrices appear to follow curves. We conjecture that, when the above average has a sufficiently regular planar density, the limiting eigenvalue measure is its mother body. We prove it for a class of finite Dirichlet discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential $V$ and a common real coefficient $α>0$ on the two adjacent diagonals. When $(\Im V)'>0$ and $V$ admits a suitable holomorphic extension, the limiting measure is supported on finitely many analytic arcs. Its logarithmic potential falls below that of the averaged measure by twice the least of four explicit actions. We obtain these actions from a four-term asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet determinant. When $\Im V$ is not monotone, an exact transfer recursion gives a conditional extension. For a circular potential arc we verify the geometric switching condition, leaving non-resonance as the remaining hypothesis.

title: High-order FEEC discretization on 2D and 3D domains with a disk-like coordinate singularity
abstract: Tensor-product splines mapped from a square to a disk-like domain form a discrete de Rham complex, but at the coordinate singularity the pushed-forward $0$-, $1$- and $2$-forms are discontinuous, unbounded and not square integrable. Existing polar constructions impose either high-order regularity on the $0$-forms only, or first-order regularity on the whole complex. For general disk-like mappings composed with a smooth diffeomorphism, we construct polar subspaces of all three tensor-product spaces that are conforming, form a cochain complex with the cohomology of the disk, and are $\mathcal{C}^{\mathfrak{r}-m}$ at the center for $m$-forms, for any $\mathfrak{r}$ up to the spline degree, under a compatibility condition between the mapping and the angular basis. The construction enriches the $2$-form space with projected polynomials and lifts them to curl-like $1$-forms by Poincaré-type homotopy operators, which reduce to cumulative sums of radial B-spline coefficients, so that the homotopy identities hold exactly. The same operators yield sparse commuting projections that preserve total flux and circulation, and boundary-compatible homotopies that solve the curl--curl problem with a single mass-matrix inversion. In 3D, the tensor product with a periodic 1D complex carries all properties over to stellarator-like solid tori. Numerical experiments confirm optimal projection accuracy and the predicted regularity, show that the regularity conditions suppress the stiff central modes of the curl--curl operator, allowing more than ten times larger time steps than first-order polar spaces, and that compatible high-order regularity is required for convergent guiding-center orbits near the axis of a discrete vacuum field.

title: Single-scale regularity from Dirichlet energy for the five-dimensional stationary Navier--Stokes equations
abstract: We establish an interior $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion for suitable weak solutions of the unforced stationary Navier--Stokes equations in an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^5$. There exists a universal constant $\varepsilon_\ast>0$ such that $x_0$ is regular if, for some ball $B_R(x_0)\subsetΩ$ with $R>0$, \[ \frac1R\int_{B_R(x_0)}|\nabla u|^2\,dx \leq \varepsilon_\ast^2. \] The main difficulty is that the Dirichlet energy controls the velocity oscillation while its mean may be arbitrarily large. Subtracting the mean introduces a large constant drift into the perturbation equation. Moreover, smallness in $H^1$ alone is insufficient to close a direct nonlinear elliptic estimate in five dimensions. We overcome these difficulties through uniform Oseen estimates and a relative-energy comparison yielding quadratic improvement of the perturbation. As a consequence, the singular set has zero one-dimensional upper Minkowski content on every compact subset of $Ω$, and hence local upper Minkowski dimension at most one.

title: Property Gamma and McDuff Factors from Shift-Similar and Houghton-like Groups
abstract: We initiate the study of von Neumann algebras of shift-similar and Houghton-like groups, introduced by Mallery and Zaremsky as analogs of self-similar and Röver-Nekrashevych groups, respectively. Given a shift-similar group $G$ of permutations of $\mathbb{N}$, one can form the Houghton-like group $H_n(G)$, a ``mashup" of the classical Houghton group $H_n$ with $G$, which acts on $X_n$, the disjoint union of $n$ copies of $\mathbb{N}$. One main result is that when $G$ and the canonical shift map $σ$ admit a joint Følner sequence for their action on $\mathbb{N}$, then both group von Neumann algebras $L(G)$ and $L(H_n(G))$ are II$_1$ factors with property Gamma and hence $G$ and $H_n(G)$ are inner amenable. More generally, let $Γ$ be an ICC group of permutations preserving the ends of $X_n$. We prove that if the natural near action on $\mathbb{N}$ of the germs of almost permutations arising from $Γ$ along some ray is amenable, then $L(Γ)$ has property Gamma; if this group of germs is itself amenable, then $L(Γ)$ is McDuff. Then we construct a shift-similar group $G$, using property (T) groups with certain actions, such that neither $G$ nor $H_n(G)$ is inner amenable. Finally, we produce extremely broad and diverse sources of shift-similar groups satisfying the joint amenability condition. These examples come from residually finite groups and from wobbling groups of a variety of metric spaces. In particular, we completely characterize all metrics $d$ on $\mathbb{N}$ for which the wobbling group $W(\mathbb{N},d)$ is shift-similar in terms of a coarse geometric property---namely, that $σ^{-1}$ is bornologous with respect to $d$. As a consequence, this gives us necessary and sufficient conditions for when the wobbling group of any countable metric space admits a shift-similar embedding.

title: Centres and semisimple deformations of contraction algebras
abstract: Let $A_{\rm{con}}$ be the contraction algebra of a $3$-fold flop of an irreducible curve, with genus-zero Gopakumar-Vafa invariants $n_1, \dots, n_l$. We show that $\prod_j M_j(\mathbb{C})^{n_j}$ is the only semisimple algebra to which $A_{\rm{con}}$ deforms. Hence $A_{\rm{con}}$ encodes its Gopakumar-Vafa invariants intrinsically, answering a question of Wemyss. Hua and Toda showed that this deformation exists, and Jelisiejew and Smoktunowicz proved its uniqueness in types A and D. The key step in our proof is that the centre of $A_{\rm{con}}$ has dimension $n_1 + \dots + n_l$. To prove this, we lift the contraction algebra of the universal flop to the Cartan subalgebra, where it becomes a corner of a deformed preprojective algebra. We show that the universal contraction algebra and its zeroth Hochschild homology are free over a polynomial ring, with presentations whose determinants are products of roots. Pulling these presentations back along the arc that classifies the flop gives the count, and recovers Toda's formula for $\dim A_{\rm{con}}$. We also prove Hua and Toda's flatness conjecture, and determine which Gopakumar-Vafa invariants occur in lengths 3 to 6.

title: Elliptic units, derived Heegner classes and the p-adic Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer quotient of CM elliptic curves of rank two
abstract: Let $E\colon y^2=x^3-Dx$ have rank two and let $p\equiv1\pmod4$ be a prime of good reduction. We study the conjecture that the $p$-adic quotient $q_p$, the leading coefficient of the cyclotomic $p$-adic $L$-function divided by the Euler factor and the $p$-adic regulator, equals the complex quotient $q_\infty=L''(E,1)/(2Ω_E\mathrm{Reg}_\infty)$, and that the latter is rational. In rank one the analogous statement is a theorem of Perrin-Riou and Rubin, because a Heegner point computes both sides; in rank two there is no such point. We show that $q_p$ is the constant of the quadratic term of the two-variable Katz measure; this is how the conjecture arises, and it computes $q_p$ modulo any power of $p$ from critical Hecke $L$-values. We then show that $q_p$ is the coordinate of two global classes: Rubin's rank-two elliptic-unit class, whose position in $E(\mathbb{Q})\otimes\mathbb{Q}_p$ is $q_p$ times an explicit vector, and the derived Heegner class over an auxiliary imaginary quadratic field $F$, for which we prove an exact identity. As consequences, whenever such a field $F$ satisfying our hypotheses exists, $q_p$ is a square in $\mathbb{Q}_p$ times the product of the Tamagawa numbers of $E$, so that the unit $q_p/A_E$ of the $p$-adic Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula is a square when Sha is finite; if moreover the derived Heegner class has non-zero formal logarithm, the conjecture of Agboola and Castella for $E/F$ holds up to a $p$-adic unit, and with a theorem of Burungale, Castella and Skinner the anticyclotomic main conjecture holds integrally; and our conjecture is equivalent to the analytic form of theirs, with the products of anticyclotomic heights read sesquilinearly, which differs by a sign from its literal formulation. The conjecture is verified modulo $p^3$ for 5520 pairs $(E,p)$ with conductors up to $3.9\cdot10^{12}$, including curves with analytic Sha of order 4 and 9.

title: Recurrent and rigid multipliers on commutative Banach algebras. The Fourier algebra
abstract: We study recurrence, rigidity and uniform rigidity of multipliers on semisimple commutative Banach algebras. For a power-bounded multiplier $T$ on a Tauberian, self-adjoint algebra $\mathfrak{A}$, we show that $T$ satisfies each of these properties if and only if the multiplication operator on $C_0(Δ(\mathfrak{A}))$ induced by the Gelfand transform of $T$ does. One consequence of our analysis is that, if $Δ(\mathfrak{A})$ is $σ$-compact, then recurrence implies rigidity for such multipliers. We examine in detail the multipliers of the Fourier algebra $A(G)$. In particular, we show that recurrence of a multiplier of $A(G)$ is equivalent to recurrence of the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ when the connected components of $G$ are open. For multipliers that are not power bounded, a flexible construction based on chains of compact subgroups of a locally compact abelian group $G$ produces multipliers of $A(G)$ that are rigid but not uniformly rigid, and multipliers that are recurrent but not rigid, such that in each case the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ is uniformly rigid. Via the Fourier-Stieltjes transform, these results describe the recurrence and rigidity properties of convolution operators on $L^1(G)$.

title: Enhanced Informed Dynamic BP Decoding Scheduling Strategies for 5G NR LDPC Codes
abstract: We present an enhanced informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) strategy to avoid propagations of unreliable messages in the residual belief-propagation (RBP) algorithm for decoding low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. To reduce the resource needed for updating the degree-one variable nodes (VNs) in an RBP-based algorithm for decoding 5G New Radio (NR) LDPC codes, we further introduce a process consisting of several simple procedures for managing the resource consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that our RBP algorithm based on the Proposed IDS strategy outperforms existing RBP-based algorithms at the early decoding iterations. By using our degree-one VN resource managing approach, the performance of both the proposed and the existing decoders is significantly improved in decoding the 5G NR codes.

title: Hecke Algebras for Minimal Equicontinuous Cantor Actions
abstract: In this work we extend the concept of Hecke algebras to a pair of a separable infinite profinite group and a closed core-free subgroup. Motivated by applications to minimal equicontinuous Cantor actions, which are characterized by such pairs, we characterize isometric *-algebra isomorphisms between such Hecke algebras by showing that they always arise as Koopman operators of homeomorphisms between the double coset spaces combined with the multiplication by some character. We then prove that two minimal equicontinuous Cantor actions with isometric isomorphic Hecke algebras have the same Steinitz order. We provide examples including the infinite dihedral group and the Grigorchuk group.

title: The multiplier step size in classical two-block ADMM: convergence and counterexamples
abstract: How large can the multiplier step be in the classical two-block alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)? We keep the penalty fixed and use the usual primal updates. We consider finite-dimensional problems with closed proper convex objectives. We assume that a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker point exists and that each block subproblem attains its minimum at every step. Under these assumptions, the constraint images and the multiplier converge for a range of factors that extends beyond the golden ratio. The constraint matrices may be rank deficient. For larger steps, we construct two fixed compact polytopes and give an explicit threshold below two. The polytopes admit an infeasible periodic orbit for every factor at or above this threshold. At that threshold, ADMM can cycle even for smooth strongly convex objectives. This gives a negative answer to Glowinski's question about the full interval from zero to two. A different pair of piecewise-quadratic objectives gives geometrically growing residuals. For the general convex class, we locate the endpoint of the uniform convergence interval near 1.88688256. A convergence certificate on the unit circle gives the lower bound, while a separate periodic orbit gives the upper bound. Exact arithmetic verifies that the two bounds differ by less than 0.000000174.

title: Second-order optimality conditions for $C^{1,1}$ sparsity constrained optimization problems via disjunctive programming
abstract: In this paper, we investigate second-order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for a class of $C^{1,1}$ sparsity constrained optimization problems via a disjunctive programming approach. More precisely, by utilizing the limiting/Mordukhovich second-order subdifferential of the associated Lagrangian function, we establish new second-order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for local optimal solutions. These results are derived under mild assumptions and extend several existing results in the literature. In addition, we apply our theoretical developments to sparse multiobjective optimization problems and derive second-order optimality conditions for efficient solutions.

title: Strong convergence rates for numerical approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation with additive rough noise
abstract: We establish strong convergence rates for a fully discrete method of the one-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive rough noise. Using the Cole-Hopf transformation, the equation is converted into a linear stochastic heat equation, which is discretized by a spectral Galerkin method in space and an accelerated exponential Euler method in time. A numerical approximation of the original solution is then reconstructed through a regularized inverse Cole-Hopf transformation. The analysis combines strong Sobolev error estimates with the positivity and inverse-moment bounds for the transformed solution. For additive space-time white noise, the numerical method achieves mean-square convergence rates arbitrarily close to 1/2 in space and 1/4 in time. The rates are slower when the noises are rougher.

title: The Sparse-Complement Conjecture for Two Distinct Eigenvalues
abstract: For a graph $G$, let $q(G)$ be the minimum number of distinct eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix whose off-diagonal zero--nonzero pattern is $G$. We prove that $q(G)=2$ whenever the complement $H=\overline G$ of a graph of order $n\ge3$ has at most $n-3$ edges, resolving the sparse-complement conjecture of Fallat and Mojallal. If $H$ contains a cycle, the proof constructs a nontrivial orthogonal projector with the strong spectral property and rank at most $|E(F)|-|V(F)|+4$, where $F$ is the union of the cyclic components of $H$. The construction combines faithful stress-free Gram representations, a one-coordinate lift for each excess core edge, exact orthogonal-frame completion, and a Stiefel-manifold pendant-extension argument.

title: Characterization of Attenuated V-Line Transform and Direct Reconstruction from Samples
abstract: The V-line transform (V-LT), a generalized Radon transform (RT), is widely used in Compton scattering imaging (CSI). The central mathematical problem of CSI is to reconstruct a function from its V-LT. Unlike V-LT, the attenuated V-line transform (AV-LT) accounts for the medium-induced loss of intensity, and has been demonstrated to improve image quality. The present paper makes two main contributions. (1) We establish the fundamental characterizations for AV-LT including operator properties ($L^2$-boundedness, operator norm etc.), a necessary and sufficient condition for the preservation of compact support, and sharp estimation of Sobolev smoothness. These characterizations remain unexplored, and they reveal essential differences among AV-LT, RT and V-LT. (2) We develop a direct reconstruction method based on AV-LT samples that does not require solving any equation. Our sampling formula gives exact reconstruction for band-limited functions. We also provide approximate reconstruction for functions in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ with $s>2$.

title: Complete uniqueness for two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows
abstract: Alt, Caffarelli and Friedman established the existence of two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows in [Asymmetric jet flows. Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 35, 29--68, 1982]. In their formulation, the constant fluid speed $λ$ on the free boundaries and the downstream asymptotic angle $θ$ are selected as part of the solution. In this paper, we prove that the asymmetric jet is unique for a prescribed nozzle and mass flux. We first establish the strict vertical monotonicity of the stream function $u$ and introduce the partial hodograph coordinates $ξ=x$ and $η=u(x,y)$, which map every fluid domain onto the same fixed strip. Under this framework, each jet is characterized by a height function $y=h(ξ,η)$, which determines the vertical position along the streamline $u=η$ at horizontal coordinate $ξ$. By analyzing the difference between the height functions of two candidate jets on this strip, we derive an elliptic equation with Dirichlet conditions on the fixed walls and conormal conditions on the free boundaries. Combining these mixed boundary conditions with the asymptotic behaviors, we first establish the uniqueness of the free-boundary fluid speed $λ$. For the resulting common speed, a local perturbation of the height function near a nozzle endpoint, together with the maximum principle, proves that the two height functions must coincide. Inverting the partial hodograph transformation then establishes the uniqueness of the physical jet.

title: Zariski dense hyperbolic 3-manifold groups in $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$
